pm.resp: Christ is ascended into heaven. Alleluia!
interc: For the Church, that she may be the faithful witness of the ascended Lord to the ends of the earth.
For our Major Archbishop, our bishop and all pastors, that they may be clothed with power from on high.
For all in authority in our nation and our state, that they may serve with justice and allow us to lead a quiet and peaceable life.
For our brothers and sisters working abroad and for families separated by distance, that the Lord may keep them.
For our families, that we may prepare with Mary in prayer for the coming of the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you have raised your Son to your right hand and given him a name above every name. Where he, our Head, has gone, let us his members follow in hope; and send us the Spirit he has promised. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Isaiah sees the Lord on his throne, is purified by a live coal, and says, “Here am I; send me!”
Acts: in the presence of Mary and the apostles, Matthias is chosen as a witness to the Resurrection.
Philippians: Christ emptied himself, and God exalted him; let the same mind be in you.
Mark: go into all the world; the Lord was taken up, and he works with those he sends.
2027-05-09.action: Offer the Lord one concrete service in your parish this week, and say to him: Here am I; send me.
2027-05-09.question: If the Lord asked me today, “Whom shall I send?”, what would I answer?
catechism: The Ascension and the right hand of the Father.
kidsaint: The prophet Isaiah

Isaiah lived in Jerusalem about seven hundred years before Jesus. One day in the Temple he saw God on a great throne, with angels singing, “Holy, holy, holy!” Isaiah felt small and sinful, but an angel touched his lips with a burning coal and made him clean. Then God asked, “Whom shall I send?” and Isaiah said, “Here am I; send me!” Isaiah wrote many beautiful promises about Jesus, the Saviour who would come. Lesson: when God asks for a helper, you can say, ‘Here I am!’
2027-05-09.special: Seventh Sunday of Resurrection, the Sunday after the Ascension. In the Latin Church in India, the Ascension of the Lord. Third day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
term: The Sanctus (Holy, holy, holy)

The hymn of the seraphs in Isaiah 6:3, sung in the Eucharistic prayer of every ancient rite. In the Syro-Malabar Qurbana it is sung in the anaphora after the priest recalls the angels who praise God; the people join the heavenly worship, and the hymn continues with “Hosanna in the highest” and “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord”. It reminds us that the Qurbana is offered before the throne of the Lord who has ascended.

family.explain: Isaiah saw God in the Temple, and he felt that he was not good enough. An angel took a burning coal from the altar and touched his lips, and Isaiah was made clean. Then God asked, “Whom shall I send?” and Isaiah said, “Here am I; send me!” Jesus too sent his friends before he went up to heaven: Go into all the world! Today Jesus asks each of us to be his helper.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, and for all who tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Where can each of us say ‘Here I am, send me’ this week: at home, at school, at work?”

illus: An illustration

At Kodungallur, where an old tradition says the apostle Thomas landed in AD 52, a group of catechism children once asked their teacher how one man from Galilee could bring the faith so far. She took them to the shore and pointed at the small fishing boats going out. ‘He came on a ship like a trader,’ she said, ‘but he carried something no trader carried. He had heard the Lord say, Go into all the world, and he believed it.’ One boy asked, ‘Who will go now?’ The teacher smiled. ‘The Lord is still asking the same question he asked Isaiah: Whom shall I send? Some of you will go across the sea. Most of you will go across the road to a neighbour. Both are the same mission.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, seated at the right hand of the Father, you send your disciples into all the world. As we gather with Mary in prayer, touch our lips and our hearts, and make us ready to be sent. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts (Isaiah 6:3). When have I felt the holiness of God, in the Qurbana or in prayer?
Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5). What do I need the Lord to purify before I can serve him?
Lord, you know everyone's heart (Acts 1:24). How do we make important decisions as a family or a group: with prayer, or without?
Let the same mind be in you that was in Christ Jesus (Philippians 2:5). Where do I seek the first place for myself?
Go into all the world and proclaim the good news (Mark 16:15). Who is the Lord sending me to this week?
pm.resp: Here am I, Lord; send me.
interc: For the Church, that in these days before Pentecost she may be renewed in her mission to all the world.
For Pope Leo and our bishops, successors of the apostles, that the Lord who knows every heart may guide them.
For missionaries from Kerala serving in India and in every continent, that the Lord may work with them and confirm their words.
For those who work in the media and social communications, that they may serve the truth and the dignity of every person.
For those who feel unworthy to serve, that the Lord may purify them and send them.
For our parish, that we may have the mind of Christ and serve one another in humility.
pm.close: Father, you exalted your Son, who emptied himself for us, and seated him at your right hand. Make us witnesses to his Resurrection, humble in our life together and generous in our mission, and send us the Holy Spirit he promised, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Exodus: at Sinai God makes Israel a priestly kingdom and a holy nation, and comes down in cloud and fire.
Acts: wind and tongues of fire; the apostles filled with the Spirit speak, and each hears in his own language.
Paul: no one can say “Jesus is Lord” except by the Holy Spirit; many gifts, one Spirit, for the common good.
Jesus: it is to your advantage that I go; the Spirit of truth will guide you into all the truth.
2027-05-16.action: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” slowly before every task today, and begin praying the Angelus again.
2027-05-16.question: What gift has the Spirit given me, and am I using it for the common good?
catechism: Pentecost reveals the Trinity and manifests the Church.
The Spirit sanctifies the Church and sends her on mission.
kidsaint: St Peter at Pentecost

Peter was a fisherman who once was so afraid that he said he did not even know Jesus. But on the day of Pentecost the Holy Spirit came like wind and fire, and Peter stood up in front of thousands of people and told them bravely that Jesus is risen! That day about three thousand people were baptised. Lesson: the Holy Spirit makes us brave to talk about Jesus!
2027-05-16.special: First Sunday of the Apostles: the Feast of Pentecost. The Season of the Apostles begins.
term: Ruha d-Qudsha

The Syriac name of the Holy Spirit, used in our liturgy (Malayalam റൂഹാദ്കുദ്ശാ). Ruha means spirit, wind and breath, like the Hebrew ruach; Qudsha means holiness. The Holy Spirit is the third Person of the Holy Trinity, “the Lord, the Giver of life, who proceeds from the Father” and is worshipped and glorified with the Father and the Son.

family.explain: After Jesus went up to heaven, his friends and Mother Mary waited and prayed in a room in Jerusalem. On the day of Pentecost they heard a sound like a strong wind, and little flames like fire came and rested on each one of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit! Then they went out and told everyone about Jesus, and people from many countries understood them in their own language. The Holy Spirit came to us too, when we were baptised.
family.intention: We pray for the whole Church, that the Holy Spirit may make us brave and loving, and for people who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing can each of us do this week with the gift the Holy Spirit has given us?”

illus: An illustration

A Syro-Malabar family from Thrissur moved to a city in the Gulf, and on their first Pentecost there they went to the big parish church. In one courtyard they heard prayers in Malayalam and Tamil, Konkani and Tagalog, Arabic and English; in the church a Holy Qurbana was being celebrated in Malayalam while another Mass was ending in another language. Their ten-year-old daughter, a little lost, asked her father, “Appa, how can it all be one Church if everyone is saying different things?” He thought for a moment and said, “Listen to the end of each prayer.” She stood near the door, and from each group she heard the same Name, said in every accent. That evening she wrote in her school diary: “Today I heard Jesus in eight languages. Pentecost is still happening.”

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful and kindle in them the fire of your love. As you came upon the apostles gathered with Mary, come upon us now. Amen. Alleluia!
share: You shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation (Exodus 19:6). How do I live as one consecrated to God?
All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:4). Where do I need the Spirit's fire in my life?
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good (1 Corinthians 12:7). What is my gift, and how can I serve with it?
He will guide you into all the truth (John 16:13). In what decision do I need the guidance of the Spirit?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, renew the face of the earth.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that the Spirit may renew her in holiness, unity and courage for mission.
For our Syro-Malabar Church at the start of the Season of the Apostles, that she may be faithful to the apostolic faith of Mar Thoma.
For all Christians, that the Spirit may lead us to the unity Christ prayed for.
For those who do not yet know Christ, that they may hear the Gospel in their own language and heart.
For the young people of our parish, that they may discover and use the gifts of the Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you sent the Spirit of your Son upon the apostles gathered with Mary. Send him upon us, make us one, distribute your gifts among us, and send us out to proclaim that Jesus is Lord. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Genesis: the Lord appears to Abraham as three visitors at Mamre; Abraham welcomes and serves them.
Isaiah: I am the first and the last; the Lord GOD has sent me and his spirit.
Romans: we have peace with God through Christ, and God's love is poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit.
John: the Spirit will take what is mine and declare it to you; all that the Father has is mine.
2027-05-23.action: Make the sign of the Cross slowly and reverently every time today, and invite one lonely person to share a meal.
2027-05-23.question: Do I live as one baptized into the life of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit?
catechism: Called to the unity of the Trinity.
kidsaint: St Patrick and the shamrock

A well-loved story says that St Patrick, who brought the Gospel to Ireland, once picked a little shamrock, a plant with three leaves on one stem, to help people understand God. Three leaves, but one shamrock: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, but one God. No picture can explain God fully, but Patrick's shamrock helped many people to pray to the Holy Trinity.
2027-05-23.special: Second Sunday of the Apostles: feast of the Most Holy Trinity. Two reading sets in the calendar: verify locally.
term: Trinity

The Church's word for the one God who is Father, Son and Holy Spirit: three distinct Persons sharing one divine nature, each wholly God. The word is not in the Bible, but the faith it names is revealed there, and the Councils of Nicaea (325) and Constantinople (381) defined it.

family.explain: Jesus told his friends that the Holy Spirit would come and teach them everything. He said, ‘All that the Father has is mine,’ and the Spirit would share it with us. God is one, but God is three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, who love each other perfectly. Each time we make the sign of the Cross we say their names. Our family is a little picture of God's love: different people, one family.
family.intention: We pray that our family may love one another as the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit love.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we make the sign of the Cross at home? Can we do it together before bed tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in Changanacherry once asked her class of nine-year-olds to explain the Holy Trinity. One boy said it was like water, ice and steam; a girl said it was like the sun, its light and its heat. Then a quiet boy at the back said, ‘I think it is like my family at night prayer. Appachan, Ammachi and I all say the same prayer, and it becomes one prayer.’ The teacher told them that every picture falls short of God, but that the last answer was close to the heart of it: God is a communion of love, and when we pray together in his Name, we are drawn into it.

pm.open: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, one God, we gather in your holy Name. Make your home among us, and let your love be poured into our hearts. Amen.
share: He looked up and saw three men standing near him (Genesis 18:2). How do I welcome God in the strangers and guests who come to me?
I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go (Isaiah 48:17). Where do I need God's guidance now?
Suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope (Romans 5:3–4). How has God brought hope out of my suffering?
He will take what is mine and declare it to you (John 16:14). What has the Holy Spirit taught me about Jesus recently?
pm.resp: Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
interc: For the Church, sign and instrument of communion with the Trinity, that she may be one as the Father and the Son are one.
For our Syro-Malabar Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may proclaim the Name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit in every land.
For families, that they may be homes of welcome and love, images of the life of God.
For those who suffer, that God's love poured out by the Spirit may give them hope that does not disappoint.
For those who doubt or seek God, that the Spirit of truth may guide them into all the truth.
pm.close: Father, through your Son and in your Holy Spirit you have opened to us your own life. Keep us in your love, guide us in your truth, and bring us at last to see you face to face, one God for ever and ever. Amen.

quick: Deuteronomy: you have stayed long enough at this mountain; resume your journey and take possession of the land.
Isaiah: the ox knows its owner and the donkey its master's crib, but my people do not understand; yet God leaves a remnant.
Paul: husband and wife belong to each other; marriage and celibacy are each a particular gift from God.
Luke: the Samaritan is moved with pity and binds the wounds; go and do likewise.
2027-05-30.action: Do one concrete act of mercy this week for someone outside your own circle.
2027-05-30.question: Whose neighbour have I refused to become?
kidsaint: St Teresa of Calcutta

Mother Teresa was a sister who taught in a school in Kolkata. One day she saw a dying man lying on the street, and no one stopped. She picked him up, washed him and cared for him, so that he could die with love. She started the Missionaries of Charity, who care for the poorest people in India and all over the world. She said that in every poor person she saw Jesus. Lesson: be like the good Samaritan, and never walk past someone who needs help!
2027-05-30.special: Third Sunday of the Apostles. Latin Church in India: Corpus Christi today.
term: Šleehe (Season of the Apostles)

The East Syriac liturgical season that begins at Pentecost and lasts about seven weeks. Šleehe means apostles: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, preached the Gospel and founded the Churches, among them the Church of India founded by Mar Thoma. Malayalam: ശ്ലീഹാക്കാലം.

family.explain: A man was walking on a lonely road when robbers beat him and left him lying there. A priest saw him and walked past. Another man walked past too. Then a Samaritan came, a man from a group the others did not like. He stopped, cleaned the man's wounds, put him on his donkey and took him to an inn to be looked after. Jesus said: “Go and do likewise.” Jesus wants us to help everyone who needs us, even people who are different from us.
family.intention: We pray for people who are hurt in road accidents, and for those who stop to help them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is someone who needs our help this week?”

illus: An illustration

Late one night on the national highway near Angamaly, a motorcyclist lay injured after a lorry had hit him and driven on. Cars slowed down, and some people took videos on their phones, but no one stopped. Then an autorickshaw driver, returning home after a long day, pulled over. He did not know the young man, who was from another district and another religion. He lifted him into the auto, drove to the hospital, gave his own phone number at the desk, and waited until the family arrived at three in the morning. When the father tried to give him money, he refused. ‘I have a son too,’ he said. Weeks later, at the young man's insistence, the two families had a meal together. The driver said afterwards, ‘At the Sunday Qurbana I had heard the story of the Samaritan many times. That night I understood that the story was waiting for me on the road.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true Samaritan, you came near to us in our wounds and healed us. Gather us now, open our eyes to see our neighbours, and send us out as your apostles. Amen.
share: You have stayed long enough at this mountain. Resume your journey (Deuteronomy 1:6–7). Where is God asking me to move on?
The ox knows its owner… but my people do not understand (Isaiah 1:3). Have I forgotten the One who feeds me?
Each has a particular gift from God (1 Corinthians 7:7). How do I honour my own vocation and that of others?
Which of these three was a neighbor? (Luke 10:36). Whom have I passed by on the other side?
pm.resp: Lord, make us neighbours to all.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may leave her comfortable mountains and carry the Gospel to all.
For married couples, especially those in difficulty, that their love may be faithful, generous and holy.
For priests and religious, that they may live their gift with joy.
For victims of accidents, violence and abandonment, and for those who stop to help them.
For India, that people of every caste, language and religion may become neighbours to one another.
pm.close: Father, your Son became our neighbour and healed our wounds. Send us on our journey with the Spirit of the apostles, bless every vocation in your Church, and make us show mercy to all, until Christ returns. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Genesis: work belonged to God's first plan; sin brought toil and sweat.
Wisdom: Solomon begs for wisdom to labour at his side.
Colossians: do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks.
Matthew: “Is not this the carpenter’s son?” The Son of God worked at Joseph's bench.
2027-05-01.action: Offer your day's work to Christ with a short prayer before you begin, and pray for one person who works far from home.
2027-05-01.question: Do I see my daily work as something I can do in the name of the Lord Jesus?
kidsaint: St Joseph the Worker

Joseph was a carpenter in the little village of Nazareth. He made tables, doors and ploughs with wood and tools. Jesus helped him in the workshop, carrying wood and learning to use the hammer and saw. Joseph worked hard so that Jesus and Mary had food and a home. When your father or mother goes to work, remember: Jesus too had a father who worked, and he helped him.
2027-05-01.special: St Joseph, Patron of the Working Class. Fifth Saturday of Resurrection. May Day.
term: Tekton
The Greek word in the Gospels for Joseph's trade, and for Jesus' own (Mark 6:3): a craftsman or builder working in wood and perhaps stone. It is usually translated ‘carpenter’.

family.explain: The people of Nazareth were surprised when Jesus taught so wisely. ‘Isn't he the carpenter's son?’ they said. Jesus grew up in Joseph's workshop and learned to work hard. St Paul tells us that whatever we do, studying, cooking, cleaning or helping, we can do it for Jesus and say thank you to God.
family.intention: We pray for all who work, for those who have no work, and for our relatives who work far away from home.
family.ask: Ask: “What work can each of us do this week for Jesus, with a happy heart?”

illus: An illustration

A carpenter in a small town near Thodupuzha kept a picture of St Joseph above his workbench. His son, who had studied engineering, once asked him why he never hurried to finish a job, even when customers were waiting. The old man ran his hand along a door he was making and said, ‘This door will open and close for fifty years. A family will go in and out through it. St Joseph made doors for Nazareth; I think one of them was opened by the hand of Jesus. I cannot do this badly.’ The son said years later that he learned more about Christian work from that answer than from any lecture.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, carpenter of Nazareth, you made holy the work of human hands. As we gather in your name, bless our homes and our labour, through the prayers of St Joseph. Amen. Alleluia!
share: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread (Genesis 3:19). What is tiring and difficult in my work just now?
That she may labor at my side (Wisdom 9:10). Where do I need God's wisdom in my work or studies?
Do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus (Colossians 3:17). How can I offer my daily work to him?
Is not this the carpenter’s son? (Matthew 13:55). Where have I failed to see God at work in ordinary people?
pm.resp: St Joseph, patron of workers, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that she may defend the dignity of every worker.
For those who have no work, and for families who struggle to live on low wages.
For workers who have come to Kerala from other states, and for our own people who work in the Gulf and across the world, that they may be treated justly and kept safe.
For employers and those in authority, that they may pay just wages and protect the weak.
For our families, that like the Holy Family of Nazareth we may work, pray and love together.
pm.close: Father, your Son was known as the carpenter's son and worked with human hands. Through the prayers of St Joseph, make our work holy, our homes peaceful and our hearts open to your Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Exodus: the song of Moses: the Lord has triumphed gloriously.
Wisdom: the despised righteous will stand with great confidence.
1 Corinthians: woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel; all things to all people.
John: I am the way, and the truth, and the life; whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
2027-05-03.action: Invite one friend to come with you to Holy Qurbana or adoration this week.
2027-05-03.question: Do I seek God in Jesus, the way, or do I look for other maps?
kidsaint: Sts Philip and James

Philip was a friend of Jesus from a fishing town. When he met Jesus, he ran to tell his friend Nathanael: ‘Come and see!’ James was another apostle who loved Jesus and led the Christians in Jerusalem. Both of them told everyone about Jesus and gave their lives for him. Today we can be like Philip: we can invite our friends to come and see Jesus.
2027-05-03.special: Sts Philip and James, Apostles. Sixth Monday of Resurrection.
term: Shliha

The Syriac word for apostle, ‘one who is sent’, like the Greek apostolos. In Malayalam we say ശ്ലീഹാ, and the Twelve are ശ്ലീഹന്മാർ. The Church is apostolic because she is built on those whom Christ sent.

family.explain: At the Last Supper Philip said to Jesus, ‘Show us the Father!’ Jesus said, ‘Philip, whoever has seen me has seen the Father.’ If we want to know what God is like, we look at Jesus: kind to children, forgiving sinners, healing the sick, giving his life for us.
family.intention: We pray for all who are searching for God, that they may find Jesus, the way.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is one friend we could invite to come and see Jesus with us?”

illus: An illustration

A college student in Ernakulam had a friend who said he no longer believed in anything. The student did not try to win an argument. One evening he simply said, ‘There is adoration at the chapel near the hostel. I go every Thursday. Come and see.’ The friend came, sat at the back, and left after ten minutes. He came again the next week, and stayed longer. Months later he told the student, ‘You never preached at me. You just took me to the place where you meet him.’ Like Philip with Nathanael, the student had learned that the best answer is often an invitation.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the way, the truth and the life. As we gather like your apostles, calm our troubled hearts and show us the Father. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Do not let your hearts be troubled (John 14:1). What is troubling my heart today?
Lord, show us the Father (John 14:8). Where am I searching for God?
Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:16). Whom is the Lord asking me to tell about him?
Come and see (John 1:46). Whom can I invite to meet Jesus?
pm.resp: Jesus, you are the way, the truth and the life.
interc: For the Pope and the bishops, successors of the apostles, that they may guard and proclaim the apostolic faith.
For the Church in India, that she may lead seekers to Christ with respect and love.
For persecuted Christians, that like the apostles they may stand with confidence.
For those whose hearts are troubled by sickness, grief or fear, that they may trust in the Father's house.
For our parish youth, that they may invite their friends to come and see.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the way to you, and in him we see your face. Through the prayers of the apostles Philip and James, keep us faithful to their witness. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: No one knows the day or hour; therefore keep alert.
The Master leaves each servant his work and the doorkeeper the watch.
Peter: we wait for new heavens and a new earth, where righteousness is at home.
2027-05-04.action: Before sleeping tonight, pray for those who will die this night, and examine how you served the Lord today.
2027-05-04.question: If the Master came this evening, would he find me awake and at my work?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who went on a long journey. He gave each of his servants a job, and he told the doorkeeper to stay awake. Nobody knew when he would come home! Jesus will come back one day, and he wants to find us ready: kind, honest and praying.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick tonight, and for all who are dying.
family.ask: Ask: “What job has Jesus given each of us in our family?”

illus: An illustration

A security guard at a hospital in Kozhikode worked the night shift for many years. Asked how he stayed awake through the long hours, he said, ‘I pray the Rosary while I walk the corridors. At about three o'clock I pass the window of the maternity ward and the window of the room where the very sick are kept. I pray for the babies being born and for the old people who may go to God before morning. Then the night does not feel long.’ Without knowing it, he had turned his duty into the watch of the Gospel.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you told us to keep awake. As we gather, rouse us from every sleep of the heart and keep us ready for your coming. Amen. Alleluia!
share: About that day or hour no one knows (Mark 13:32). How do I live, knowing that I do not know the day?
Each with his work (Mark 13:34). What work has the Lord given me in his house?
Keep awake (Mark 13:37). Where have I fallen asleep spiritually?
We wait for new heavens and a new earth (2 Peter 3:13). How can I care for God's creation while I wait?
pm.resp: Come, Lord Jesus.
interc: For the Church, that she may watch and pray until the Lord returns.
For those who will die this night, that they may be found ready.
For night workers, nurses, watchmen and drivers, that the Lord may keep them.
For our land, our rivers and hills, that we may care for them as faithful stewards.
For ourselves, that we may be awake and at our work when the Master comes.
pm.close: Father, you alone know the day and the hour. Keep us faithful in our work and watchful in prayer, waiting for the new heavens and the new earth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Jesus wants his joy in us; it is found in loving as he loved.
I have called you friends; I chose you to bear fruit that will last.
Paul: be imitators of God; instead of vulgar talk, let there be thanksgiving.
2027-05-05.action: Do one hidden act of self-giving love today, and thank God for three gifts before you sleep.
2027-05-05.question: Do I relate to Jesus as a fearful servant or as a friend who shares his heart and his work?

family.explain: Jesus said to his disciples, ‘You are my friends.’ He also says it to us! A good friend shares secrets, helps when things are hard, and is happy when we are happy. Jesus is that kind of friend. He even gave his life for us. He asks us to love each other the way he loves us.
family.intention: We pray for our friends, and for children who have no friends.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be a good friend to someone this week, the way Jesus is a friend to us?”

illus: An illustration

A teacher at a school in Changanassery noticed that a new boy from another state ate his lunch alone every day. She did not lecture the class. She simply asked one of her students, a quiet girl, to sit with the new boy and help him with Malayalam. Within a month there was a small group at that lunch table. At the end of the year the boy wrote in a card, ‘In this school I found friends.’ The girl later said that she had only tried to do what Jesus did when he called ordinary people his friends.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us your friends. As we gather in your name, let your joy be in us and teach us to love one another as you have loved us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: So that my joy may be in you (John 15:11). Where do I find true joy?
Love one another as I have loved you (John 15:12). Whom do I find it hard to love?
I have called you friends (John 15:15). How is my friendship with Jesus?
Let there be thanksgiving (Ephesians 5:4). What can I thank God for today?
pm.resp: Jesus, our friend, teach us to love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be known by the love of her members for one another.
For young people, that they may keep their hearts and words clean and find true friends.
For those who are lonely, especially migrants and the elderly, that they may find friendship.
For families, that thanksgiving may fill our homes in place of quarrelling.
For all of us, that we may prepare our hearts for the feast of the Ascension tomorrow.
pm.close: Father, your Son has called us friends and chosen us to bear fruit that will last. Make us imitators of you, as beloved children, living in love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: The day after the Ascension: the One who comes from above is above all.
He gives the Spirit without measure: the nine days of prayer for Pentecost begin.
Paul: forgetting what lies behind, I press on toward the goal of the upward call of God.
2027-05-07.action: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit today, and pray it with Mary for nine days.
2027-05-07.question: Am I standing still, looking at what lies behind, or straining forward toward the Lord who has gone ahead?
catechism: Mary prays with the apostles for the Spirit.
kidsaint: St Margaret Mary Alacoque

Margaret Mary was a sister in a convent at Paray-le-Monial in France. In the 1670s, while she prayed before the Blessed Sacrament, Jesus showed her his Heart burning with love for people. He asked that people receive Holy Communion on the First Friday of the month to love him and to make up for the times he is forgotten. That is why many families go to Holy Qurbana on First Fridays! Lesson: Jesus' Heart is full of love for you; you can love him back.
2027-05-07.special: Sixth Friday of Resurrection. First Friday. The day after the Ascension (Thursday 6 May); the novena to the Holy Spirit begins.
term: Novena

Nine days of prayer for one intention, from the Latin novem, ‘nine’. The Church sees the first novena in the nine days between the Ascension and Pentecost, when the apostles prayed together with Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14) and received the Holy Spirit. The novena to the Holy Spirit, prayed from the Friday after the Ascension to the eve of Pentecost, keeps that pattern.

family.explain: Yesterday we remembered how Jesus went up to heaven. Before he went, he promised to send the Holy Spirit. So the disciples went into a room in Jerusalem and prayed with Mary, Jesus' mother, for nine days. Today the Gospel says that God gives the Spirit ‘without measure’: not a little cup, but a whole river! For nine days we too can pray with Mary: Come, Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for our family, that the Holy Spirit may fill our home with love and peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift do we want the Holy Spirit to give our family at Pentecost?” Write it on a paper and keep it near the family altar until Pentecost.

illus: An illustration

At a school sports day in Thrissur, a girl running the third leg of the relay slipped on the first bend and fell. Her knee was bleeding and her team was suddenly last. She could have sat on the track and cried over the fall. Instead she got up, forgot the bend behind her and ran with all her strength toward the next runner, who was standing with her hand stretched back. The team did not win, but the whole ground stood up and clapped as she passed the baton. Paul says that the Christian life is like that: forgetting what lies behind, we run toward the hand stretched out to us, the hand of the Lord who has gone ahead.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have gone up to the Father and you give the Spirit without measure. As we begin these nine days, gather us with Mary your Mother in prayer, and pour out your Spirit on us. Amen. Alleluia!
share: The one who comes from above is above all (John 3:31). Is Jesus truly above all in my life, or is he one concern among many?
He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). What do I most need to ask from the Holy Spirit in this novena?
Forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead (Philippians 3:13). What past failure or hurt do I keep carrying?
They were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). How can our group pray together until Pentecost?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.
interc: For the Church, gathered in prayer as in the upper room, that she may receive the Spirit anew at Pentecost.
For our Syro-Malabar Church, our bishops, priests and religious, that the Spirit may renew their zeal.
For those who are tired and have stopped running, that the Lord may lift them up and set their face toward the goal.
For those who keep the First Friday today, that the Heart of Jesus may heal and strengthen them.
For our families, that we may pray together with Mary in these nine days.
pm.close: Father, your Son has gone up to you and has placed all things in your hands. Through his pierced Heart, pour out on us the Spirit without measure, that we may run toward the upward call you have given us in Christ Jesus our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: John the Baptist: bear fruit worthy of repentance; God looks for fruit, not family trees.
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire: the promise fulfilled at Pentecost.
Paul: an undivided heart and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
2027-05-08.action: Choose one concrete fruit of conversion for this week, and pray the novena with Mary today.
2027-05-08.question: What chaff in my life do I need the fire of the Spirit to blow away?
kidsaint: St Euphrasia

Rose Eluvathingal was born in 1877 at Kattoor near Thrissur. As a girl she wanted to belong only to Jesus, and she became a sister of the Congregation of the Mother of Carmel, taking the name Euphrasia. At the convent in Ollur she prayed so much that people called her the ‘praying mother’. She died in 1952, and Pope Francis declared her a saint in 2014. Lesson: a heart that belongs to Jesus has room for everyone who needs prayer.
2027-05-08.special: Sixth Saturday of Resurrection. A Saturday of the Marian month of May; second day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
term: Winnowing

The old way of separating grain from husk: the threshed crop is tossed into the wind with a winnowing fork or a flat basket, so that the light chaff blows away and the heavy grain falls. John the Baptist uses the picture for the judgment of the Messiah, and the Church sees in it the work of the Holy Spirit, who separates what is empty from what is good.

family.explain: John the Baptist baptized people in the river Jordan with water. But he said: someone greater is coming, and he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire! Fire gives light and warmth, and it makes things clean. At Pentecost the Holy Spirit came on the disciples like little flames of fire. The Holy Spirit wants to make our hearts warm with love and bright with goodness.
family.intention: We pray for priests and sisters, who give their whole heart to Jesus, and for all families.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one good fruit our family can give God this week?”

illus: An illustration

An old farmer in Kuttanad used to winnow the paddy by hand long after machines came to the village. His grandson once asked why he waited for the evening wind instead of finishing in the morning. The old man lifted a basket of grain, let it fall slowly, and the husk flew away over the bund while the grain dropped at his feet. ‘The wind knows what is heavy and what is empty,’ he said. ‘I only have to lift it up.’ In these days before Pentecost we lift up our hearts to the Wind of God. What is empty in us he blows away; what is good he gathers.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, fire of God, come upon us as we gather. With Mary, who prayed with the apostles for your coming, we open our hearts to you. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Bear fruit worthy of repentance (Matthew 3:8). What fruit is the Lord looking for in my life now?
Do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our ancestor’ (Matthew 3:9). On what do I rely instead of real conversion?
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire (Matthew 3:11). What would I like the Spirit's fire to change in me?
Unhindered devotion to the Lord (1 Corinthians 7:35). What divides my heart?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, kindle in us the fire of your love.
interc: For the Church, that she may be renewed by the fire of the Spirit at Pentecost.
For priests and religious, that they may serve with undivided hearts.
For married couples, that their love may be holy and faithful.
For young people discerning their call, that they may hear the Lord and answer generously.
For all who rely on their past instead of turning to God today, that they may bear fruit.
pm.close: Father, your Son promised to baptize us with the Holy Spirit and fire. Through the prayers of the Virgin Mary, send your Spirit to make our hearts whole and our lives fruitful, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: At Jacob's well the tired Lord asks a Samaritan woman for a drink, crossing every wall.
He promises living water: the Spirit, a spring gushing up to eternal life.
Paul: God chose you as first fruits; stand firm and hold fast to the traditions.
2027-05-10.action: Tell the Lord honestly what you are thirsty for, and offer a drink to someone in his name.
2027-05-10.question: From which wells am I trying to quench a thirst that only God can satisfy?
kidsaint: The Samaritan woman

The Gospel does not tell us her name; an old Eastern tradition calls her Photini, which means ‘the shining one’. She came to the well at noon to draw water, and she met Jesus, who asked her for a drink. When she understood who he was, she left her water jar and ran to tell the whole town, ‘Come and see!’ Many people believed because of her. Lesson: when you meet Jesus, you can say to your friends, ‘Come and see!’
2027-05-10.special: Seventh Monday of Resurrection. Fourth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, St John of Avila.
term: Tradition

From the Latin traditio, ‘handing on’ (in Greek paradosis). The Church's living transmission of the Gospel received from the apostles, in her teaching, life and worship, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit. With Sacred Scripture it forms one deposit of the faith. Paul asks the Thessalonians to hold fast to what they were taught “either by word of mouth or by our letter”.

family.explain: Jesus was tired and thirsty, and he sat beside a well. A woman came to draw water, and Jesus asked her, ‘Please give me a drink.’ Then he told her about a special water that he gives: whoever drinks it will never be thirsty again! This water is the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with God's love. In a few days, at Pentecost, we will celebrate the coming of the Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for people who have no clean water to drink, and for all who are thirsty for God's love.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we give a glass of water or a kind word to this week?”

illus: An illustration

In an old house near Pala there is a well that the family says has never dried, not even in the drought summers when the river shrank to a stream. Neighbours came with pots, and the grandmother never sent anyone away. Once a city cousin asked why the well stayed full. The old woman said, ‘The water does not come from the top. It comes from a spring underneath that we cannot see.’ Jesus promised that the Holy Spirit would be like that in us: not a bucket of water that runs out, but a hidden spring, ‘gushing up to eternal life’, from which others too can drink.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you sat tired by the well and asked for a drink. We come to you thirsty; give us the living water of your Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Jesus, tired out by his journey, was sitting by the well (John 4:6). How does it move me that the Lord knows tiredness?
If you knew the gift of God (John 4:10). What gift of God have I not yet understood or received?
Everyone who drinks of this water will be thirsty again (John 4:13). What wells do I keep going back to that leave me thirsty?
Stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught (2 Thessalonians 2:15). Which tradition of our Church helps me most to stay close to God?
pm.resp: Lord, give us this water.
interc: For the Church, that she may offer the living water of Christ to all who thirst.
For those who are tired of life and have lost hope, that the Spirit may become a spring of new life in them.
For people divided by religion, caste or community, that the example of Jesus at the well may teach us to cross walls with respect.
For those who lack clean water, and for all who work to provide it.
For our families, that we may hand on the faith of our fathers with joy.
pm.close: Father, your Son gives the living water that quenches every thirst. Pour out your Spirit on us, keep us faithful to the faith handed down from the apostles, and comfort our hearts with good hope, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Jesus refuses to divide an inheritance but warns: be on your guard against all kinds of greed.
The rich fool talks only to himself; God says, This very night your life is demanded of you.
Paul: knowledge puffs up, love builds up; do not cause the weak, for whom Christ died, to stumble.
2027-05-11.action: Give away one thing you have stored and do not use, and take one step toward peace in any family quarrel over property.
2027-05-11.question: Am I storing up treasure for myself, or am I rich toward God?
kidsaint: Blessed Kunjachan

Father Augustine Thevarparampil, whom everyone called Kunjachan (‘little father’) because he was short, was a priest of Ramapuram in Kerala. He spent his whole life visiting poor Dalit families, walking from house to house, teaching them to pray, caring for the sick and treating everyone as a child of God at a time when many looked down on them. He owned almost nothing, but he was rich toward God. He died in 1973 and was beatified in 2006. Lesson: the best treasure is the love we give away.
2027-05-11.special: Seventh Tuesday of Resurrection. Fifth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit.
term: Scandal

In the Bible the skandalon is a stumbling block, something placed on the path that makes another fall. In Christian moral teaching scandal is an attitude or behaviour that leads another person to sin. Paul refuses to use even his rightful liberty if it would make a weaker believer fall (1 Corinthians 8:13); Jesus speaks severe words against those who cause the little ones to stumble.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a rich farmer who had so much grain that he built bigger and bigger barns. He thought only about himself: ‘I will eat, drink and be happy!’ He never thought of God or of hungry people. But that night his life came to an end, and all his grain was left behind. Jesus says we should be ‘rich toward God’: sharing what we have and loving others.
family.intention: We pray for families who quarrel over money or land, that they may make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share this week with someone who has less than we do?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in Kottayam did not speak for eleven years because of a strip of land between their houses, hardly five cents. Each was sure the plot was his. When their mother was dying, she asked them to come together to her bed and said only one thing: ‘I did not raise you to fight over mud.’ After the funeral the elder brother came to the younger with the documents and said, ‘Let neither of us have it.’ Together they gave the land to the parish, and with the help of neighbours a small house was built there for a widow and her children. The brothers say that the day the keys were handed over was the first day in eleven years they had laughed together.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you became poor to make us rich. As we gather in your name, loosen the grip of money on our hearts and open them to your Spirit. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Be on your guard against all kinds of greed (Luke 12:15). Where does greed hide in my life?
I will pull down my barns and build larger ones (Luke 12:18). What am I storing up that I could share?
This very night your life is being demanded of you (Luke 12:20). If my life were asked of me tonight, what would I wish I had done?
Take care that this liberty of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak (1 Corinthians 8:9). Has my behaviour ever made someone weaker stumble?
pm.resp: Lord, make us rich toward you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be poor in spirit and generous to all in need.
For families divided by quarrels over property and inheritance, that they may be reconciled.
For the rich and powerful, that they may use their goods for the common good.
For young people and all whose faith is fragile, that no one may cause them to stumble.
For the poor of our parish, that we may share with them as brothers and sisters.
pm.close: Father, every good gift comes from you. Teach us to hold our goods with open hands, to share them with the poor and to protect the weak, so that we may be rich toward you, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Jesus prays: Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son. The Ascended Lord still intercedes for us.
This is eternal life: to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent.
John: God is love; he has given us of his Spirit; perfect love casts out fear; love the brother you can see.
2027-05-12.action: Read John 17 slowly this week, and do one concrete act of love today for someone you find difficult.
2027-05-12.question: Is my faith ruled more by fear of God or by trust in his love?
kidsaint: St Pancras

Pancras was a boy who lived in Rome about three hundred years after Jesus. The old stories say that he became a Christian as a young teenager. When the emperor ordered Christians to give up their faith, Pancras, though he was only about fourteen, said that he would not deny Jesus, and he was put to death. A great church in Rome is named after him. Lesson: perfect love casts out fear; when we love Jesus, he makes us brave.
2027-05-12.special: Seventh Wednesday of Resurrection. Sixth day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, Sts Nereus and Achilleus and St Pancras.
term: High-priestly prayer

The name given since the sixteenth century to the prayer of Jesus in John 17, spoken at the Last Supper on the night before his Passion. In it Jesus prays for his own glorification, for his disciples and for all who will believe through their word, “that they may all be one”. It is the prayer of the High Priest who offers himself, and he continues it in heaven, where he “always lives to make intercession” for us (Hebrews 7:25).

family.explain: John tells us something wonderful: God is love! He loves us so much that he gives us his Holy Spirit, and when we love one another, God lives in us. John also says, ‘There is no fear in love.’ We do not need to be afraid of God; he is our Father who loves us. ‘We love because he first loved us.’
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid, that they may feel God's love.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is one person in our family or class we can show God's love to tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration

A young doctor from Changanacherry remembers how, as a boy, he was afraid of God. He thought of him as a stern headmaster with a book of marks. What changed him was not a sermon but his grandmother. Every evening at dusk she sat on the verandah with her rosary, talking to God and to Mary as if they were sitting beside her, sometimes laughing, sometimes crying, always at peace. One night he asked her, ‘Ammachi, are you not afraid of God?’ She looked at him in surprise. ‘Afraid? Monae, I have known him for eighty years.’ That, he says, was the first time he understood that eternal life is to know God, and that the more you know him, the less you fear.

pm.open: Father, your Son prayed for us on the night before he died, and he intercedes for us still. Pour your love into our hearts by the Holy Spirit as we gather. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Father, the hour has come (John 17:1). What “hour” of difficulty am I living, and can I see God's glory in it?
This is eternal life, that they may know you (John 17:3). Do I know God, or only know about him?
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). What fear keeps me from trusting God?
Those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen (1 John 4:20). Whom do I find hardest to love?
pm.resp: Lord, abide in us, and let us abide in your love.
interc: For the Church, that her members may know the Father and the Son and live in love.
For Christians who live in fear of God, that they may discover his love.
For those who are persecuted for the faith, like the young martyrs of Rome, that perfect love may cast out their fear.
For families and communities divided by hatred, that the Spirit may make them one.
For our parish, that our love for God may be seen in our love for one another.
pm.close: Father, you are love, and you have given us your Spirit. Let us know you and your Son, abide in your love and love one another, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: John: we declare to you what we have heard, seen and touched, the word of life, so that you may have fellowship with us and with the Father and the Son.
Jesus: whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple; no love may take his place.
Count the cost like the builder and the king; salt that loses its taste is thrown away.
2027-05-13.action: Finish one Christian commitment you have left half done, and restore one family practice that has lost its taste.
2027-05-13.question: Am I a member of the crowd that follows for a day, or a disciple who follows to the end?
catechism: Witness to what we have seen and heard.
Family ties and the first vocation.
kidsaint: Sts Francisco and Jacinta Marto

Francisco and Jacinta were a brother and sister from a poor village near Fatima in Portugal. On 13 May 1917, while they were looking after sheep with their cousin Lucia, Our Lady appeared to them and asked them to pray the rosary every day and to make little sacrifices for sinners. They did it with all their heart, even when people did not believe them. Both died young, Francisco in 1919 and Jacinta in 1920, and Pope Francis declared them saints at Fatima on 13 May 2017. Lesson: even children can pray and offer sacrifices for the world.
2027-05-13.special: Seventh Thursday of Resurrection. Seventh day of the novena to the Holy Spirit. In the Latin calendar, Our Lady of Fatima.
term: Fellowship (koinonia)

The Greek word koinonia means sharing, communion, having something in common. John uses it for the life the apostles share with the Father and the Son, and which they open to all who receive their witness (1 John 1:3). The first believers in Jerusalem “devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers” (Acts 2:42). It is the communion of the Church, made by the Holy Spirit.

family.explain: Jesus said that following him is like building a tall tower. Before you start, you sit down and think: do I have enough bricks and money to finish it? Otherwise people will laugh: ‘He started but could not finish!’ Jesus wants us to follow him all the way, even when it is hard, like carrying a cross. The Holy Spirit gives us the strength to keep going.
family.intention: We pray for people who started following Jesus and have stopped, that they may come back.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a good thing we started as a family and did not finish? Let us finish it!”

illus: An illustration

On a roadside near Thodupuzha there stands a house that was never finished. The pillars of the first floor rise into the sky with their iron rods rusting in the rain, and grass grows on the roof slab. Neighbours say that the owner began to build it with great plans and a loan he could not repay. Every child who passes asks the same question: ‘Who started that house?’ Jesus said that discipleship is like that: it is easy to lay a foundation in a moment of enthusiasm, at a retreat, on the day of First Holy Communion, and much harder to build to the roof. The Holy Spirit is given to the Church so that the towers we begin may be finished.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Word of life, we have heard of you and received you. Gather us in fellowship with the Father and with you, and give us courage to follow you to the end. Amen. Alleluia!
share: What we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands (1 John 1:1). How have I “touched” the Lord in my life?
Whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother … cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:26). Is any love in my life taking the place of Christ?
Which of you, intending to build a tower, does not first sit down and estimate the cost? (Luke 14:28). What Christian commitment have I started and not finished?
Salt is good; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored? (Luke 14:34). Where has my faith lost its taste?
pm.resp: Lord, give us strength to follow you to the end.
interc: For the Church, that she may declare with joy what the apostles saw and heard.
For those who have lost the taste of faith, that the Spirit may renew them.
For families, that they may love one another deeply and love Christ above all.
For peace in the world and the conversion of sinners, as Our Lady asked at Fatima.
For children and young people, that like Francisco and Jacinta they may pray generously.
pm.close: Father, through the witness of the apostles you have called us into fellowship with you and your Son. Give us the Spirit, that we may carry our cross, finish what we have begun and be salt for the earth, through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Samuel: the LORD looks on the heart; the youngest son, keeping the sheep, is anointed.
Acts: the praying Church chooses Matthias to be a witness to the Resurrection with the eleven.
Paul: God chose what is weak in the world, so that no one might boast before God.
Jesus: revealed to infants; come to me and I will give you rest.
2027-05-14.action: Before one decision today, pray: Lord, you know the heart; show me what you have chosen.
2027-05-14.question: Do I judge people by appearance, or try to see them as the Lord sees the heart?
catechism: The Twelve, foundation of the new Israel.
The Church built on the apostles.
kidsaint: St Matthias

After Judas left, there were only eleven apostles, and Jesus had chosen twelve. So the friends of Jesus prayed together with Mother Mary, and asked God to show them who should be the twelfth. They chose Matthias, a man who had followed Jesus from the very beginning and had seen him risen. Lesson: God sees our heart, and he can choose anyone who loves Jesus faithfully!
2027-05-14.special: St Matthias, Apostle (Mar Mathias Shleeha). Seventh Friday of Resurrection.
term: Apostle (Shleeha)

From the Greek apostolos and the Syriac shlīḥā, both meaning one who is sent. The Twelve were chosen by Jesus to be with him and to be sent out as witnesses of his Resurrection; our Church calls them Shleehe, and the Season of the Apostles that begins at Pentecost bears their name. The bishops are their successors.

family.explain: After Jesus went up to heaven, his friends waited in Jerusalem and prayed with Mother Mary. One place among the twelve apostles was empty, because Judas had left. Peter said they needed someone who had walked with Jesus from the beginning and had seen him alive after Easter. They prayed: “Lord, you know everyone’s heart.” Then God showed them Matthias. God sees what is inside us, not only what is outside.
family.intention: We pray for our bishops and priests, that they may be faithful witnesses of Jesus like the apostles.
family.ask: Ask: “When we have to decide something as a family, do we first pray and ask God what he wants?”

illus: An illustration

In 2012 the Coptic Orthodox Church of Egypt chose a new Pope in the ancient way. After much prayer, the names of three candidates were placed in a sealed box on the altar, and during the liturgy a small boy, blindfolded, drew out one name. The man chosen, Bishop Tawadros, accepted it as the Lord's choice. Many watching in Egypt wept as the name was read. It was the scene of Acts 1 repeated: a Church at prayer, a decision placed in the Lord's hands, and a chosen servant who did not choose himself.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you chose your apostles and you know every heart. As we gather in your name with your Mother, make us one in prayer like the Church in the upper room. Amen. Alleluia!
share: Lord, you know everyone’s heart (Acts 1:24). What does the Lord see in my heart today?
One of these must become a witness with us to his resurrection (Acts 1:22). Where am I called to witness to the Risen Lord?
The LORD does not see as mortals see (1 Samuel 16:7). Whom have I judged by appearance?
Come to me, all you that are weary (Matthew 11:28). What burden do I want to give to Jesus tonight?
pm.resp: Lord, you know our hearts; show us your will.
interc: For our Major Archbishop, our bishops and all successors of the apostles, that they may be faithful witnesses of the Risen Lord.
For those preparing for priesthood and religious life, that they may hear the Lord's choice and answer with joy.
For those who have been passed over or forgotten, that they may know God's love for them.
For all who are weary and burdened, that they may find rest in Christ.
For our families and parishes, that we may pray together as we wait for the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you completed the number of the apostles by choosing Matthias in the place of Judas. Number us also among the faithful witnesses of your Son, and fill us with the Holy Spirit whom we await. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Exodus: keep the festival of harvest, the first fruits of your labour; it is the festival of Pentecost.
Joel: the threshing floors full of grain, and the promise: I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.
Romans: the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable; God is merciful to all.
Jesus: it is not the Father's will that one of these little ones should be lost.
2027-05-15.action: Pray the rosary today for farmers and for one person who has drifted away, and prepare your heart for Pentecost.
2027-05-15.question: Is the soil of my heart ready for the rain of the Holy Spirit tomorrow?
catechism: Pentecost, the fulfilment of the Passover.
No little one is to be lost.
kidsaint: Mary, Protectress of the Harvest

Long ago Christians in faraway lands asked Mother Mary to take care of their fields when the wheat was ready to be cut. Mary is the mother who gave us Jesus, the Bread of life. She cares for farmers, for the rain and the crops, and most of all for every child of God. Lesson: we can ask Mother Mary to look after our food, our families and our friends who are far from Jesus!
2027-05-15.special: Blessed Virgin Mary, Protectress of Harvest. Seventh Saturday of Resurrection; eve of Pentecost.
term: Feast of Weeks (Pentecost)

The harvest festival of Israel, kept seven weeks (fifty days) after Passover, when the first loaves of the new wheat were offered to God (Leviticus 23:15–17). Greek-speaking Jews called it Pentecost, the fiftieth day. On this feast the Holy Spirit came down on the apostles (Acts 2:1), and the Church celebrates it as the fulfilment of Easter.

family.explain: God promised his people that after a time of hunger the rain would come again and the barns would be full of grain. Then he promised something even better: he would pour out his Holy Spirit on everyone, on boys and girls, on grandparents and young people. Tomorrow is Pentecost, the day God kept that promise. Mother Mary prayed for the Holy Spirit with the apostles. Today we ask her to take care of the farmers and the rain, and to help us get ready for the Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for farmers, for good rain in its season, and for families who do not have enough to eat.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we can thank God for that comes from the earth, every day on our table?”

illus: An illustration

In a village in Kuttanad an old farmer used to bring a small bundle of the first paddy from his field to the church every year and lay it before the statue of Mother Mary. His grandson, back from studies in the city, once asked him why, since the harvest came from fertilisers and pumps, not from the statue. The old man smiled. “The fertiliser feeds the paddy,” he said. “But who feeds my heart when the flood takes the crop? I bring her the first sheaf because she gave the world its Bread.” Years later, after the floods of 2018 had covered the fields, the grandson found himself carrying the first bundle of the new crop to the same statue. He said he finally understood that his grandfather had not been asking for a good harvest only. He had been giving thanks for a Mother who stays with you in every season.

pm.open: Holy Mother of God, Protectress of Harvest, pray with us as you prayed with the apostles. Come, Holy Spirit, upon our hearts and our land. Amen. Alleluia!
share: You shall observe the festival of harvest, of the first fruits of your labor (Exodus 23:16). What first fruits can I offer to God?
I will pour out my spirit on all flesh (Joel 2:28). What do I most need the Holy Spirit to do in me this Pentecost?
The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable (Romans 11:29). How has God been faithful to me even when I was not?
It is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost (Matthew 18:14). Whom do I need to go and search for?
pm.resp: Mother of God, pray for us; Come, Holy Spirit.
interc: For farmers in Kerala and in all India, that the monsoon may come in its season and their work be blessed.
For those who suffer from drought, flood and hunger, that they may receive help and hope.
For the Jewish people, first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For children and young people who have drifted from faith, that the Good Shepherd may find them.
For our parish, that tomorrow the Holy Spirit may renew us as on the first Pentecost.
pm.close: Father, Lord of the harvest, you gave us the Virgin Mary as the good soil from which your Son came forth. Through her prayers, bless our land and our labour, gather in the lost, and pour out your Spirit on all flesh. Through Christ our Lord. Amen. Alleluia!

quick: Mary, given to us at the Cross, is honoured today as Mother of the Church, on the day after Pentecost.
Paul: let all things be done for building up; God is a God not of disorder but of peace.
Jesus: learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest.
2027-05-17.action: Pray a decade of the rosary with your family, entrusting your home to the Mother of the Church.
2027-05-17.question: Do my words in the family and the parish build up, or do they add to the noise?
catechism: Mary at prayer in the upper room.
Gifts discerned for the common good.
kidsaint: Mary, Mother of the Church

When Jesus was on the Cross, he looked at his mother and his friend John and said to John, “Here is your mother.” From that day Mary was John's mother too, and she is the mother of all of us who belong to Jesus. After Jesus went to heaven, she prayed with his friends until the Holy Spirit came. Lesson: we have a Mother in heaven who prays for us every day!

family.explain: When Jesus was dying on the Cross, his mother Mary was standing close by, with John, his friend. Jesus gave Mary to John as his mother, and gave John to Mary as her son. Jesus gave Mary to all of us too. She is the Mother of the Church, the big family of Jesus. Yesterday was Pentecost, the birthday of the Church, and today we thank God for giving the Church a Mother.
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are tired or sad, and for children who have no mother to care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make our home a place where Mother Mary feels welcome?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Kottayam two groups in the prayer meeting had been quarrelling for months over who should lead the singing and the intercessions. One evening an elderly widow, who rarely spoke, stood up with her rosary in her hand and said only this: “At the wedding in Cana, Mother Mary said five words to the servants. ‘Do whatever he tells you.’ Then she was silent, and the water became wine.” She sat down. Nobody said anything for a long while. Then the leaders of the two groups agreed to take turns, one week each, and to begin every meeting with a decade of the rosary for the other. The prayer meeting did not become perfect, but it became peaceful.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you gave us your Mother from the Cross. With Mary, Mother of the Church, we gather in your name; send your Spirit of peace upon us. Amen.
share: Here is your mother (John 19:27). Have I welcomed Mary into my home and my life?
Let all things be done for building up (1 Corinthians 14:26). Do my words in the community build up?
God is a God not of disorder but of peace (1 Corinthians 14:33). Where do I need God's peace in my family or parish?
Learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart (Matthew 11:29). What burden do I need to bring to Jesus?
pm.resp: Mother of the Church, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, born of the Spirit at Pentecost, that under Mary's care she may grow in holiness and unity.
For our parish assemblies and prayer groups, that every gift may serve to build up and not to divide.
For mothers, especially those who are tired, ill or grieving.
For all who are weary and burdened, that they may find rest in Christ.
For those who have no one to care for them, that they may know the love of the Mother of the Church.
pm.close: Father, at the Cross your Son gave us his Mother as our own. Through her prayers keep your Church in peace and unity, and teach us to learn from the gentle and humble heart of Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Two blind men cry out, Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David, and shout louder when silenced.
Jesus stands still, asks what they want, is moved with compassion and touches their eyes; they follow him.
Paul: your faith is growing and your love increasing; may God make you worthy of his call.
2027-05-18.action: Pray the Jesus Prayer ten times today, slowly, especially when you feel discouraged.
2027-05-18.question: What is the blindness I most need Jesus to heal, and am I ready to follow him when he does?

family.explain: Two blind men were sitting by the road when Jesus was passing. They shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us!” People told them to keep quiet, but they shouted even louder. Jesus stopped, called them and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?” They said, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.” Jesus felt great love for them, touched their eyes, and they could see! Then they walked with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who are blind or have weak eyes, and for those who cannot yet see how much God loves them.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something we want to ask Jesus for, as a family, like the blind men did?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Pala lost most of her sight to an illness of the eyes in her seventies. Her grandchildren expected her to become bitter; instead she learned the Jesus Prayer from a priest who visited her and began to pray it all day, on her rosary beads, while sitting on the veranda. Neighbours started to come and sit with her, first out of kindness, then because they found peace there. A young man struggling with drink came every evening for months. When he was finally sober, he told her, “Teacher, you cannot see me, but you were the first person who saw me as someone worth praying for.” She laughed and said, “Jesus stood still for blind people. I only learned to stand still with him.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on us. As we gather in your name, open the eyes of our hearts and touch us with your compassion. Amen.
share: They shouted even more loudly, “Have mercy on us, Lord, Son of David!” (Matthew 20:31). What voices try to silence my prayer?
What do you want me to do for you? (Matthew 20:32). What would I answer Jesus tonight?
Your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing (2 Thessalonians 1:3). Where do I see faith and love growing in our community?
That our God will make you worthy of his call (2 Thessalonians 1:11). How is God calling me in this season?
pm.resp: Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that her eyes may be opened to see Christ and follow him.
For Christians who suffer persecution, that they may remain steadfast in faith and love.
For the blind and visually impaired, and for those who care for them.
For those whose hearts are blind through sin, addiction or despair, that the Lord may stand still and touch them.
For our prayer group, that our faith may grow and our love for one another increase.
pm.close: Father, your Son had compassion on the blind and opened their eyes. Open the eyes of our hearts, make us worthy of your call, and let us follow Jesus on his way. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The kingdom is like a mustard seed, the smallest seed, which becomes a tree where birds nest.
It is like yeast mixed into three measures of flour until all is leavened.
Paul: judge yourselves before the Lord's Supper, and when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
2027-05-19.action: Begin one small good thing today and trust God with its growth.
2027-05-19.question: Am I yeast that is mixed into the world around me, or do I keep my faith apart from my daily life?

family.explain: Jesus said that the kingdom of God is like a tiny mustard seed. It is so small you can hardly see it, but it grows into a big plant, and birds come to build nests in it. It is also like a little yeast that a woman puts into flour, and soon the whole dough rises. The Church began with only a few friends of Jesus, and now it is everywhere in the world, even in our village. Small things done with love can grow very big with God.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries who plant the Gospel in new places, and for small Christian communities that feel weak.
family.ask: Ask: “What small good thing can each of us start this week?”

illus: An illustration

In the 1970s a nursing sister from Kerala was sent to a village in the north of India where there were no Christians. She had a small dispensary, a bicycle and a rosary. For years she treated fevers and delivered babies, and almost no one asked about her faith. When she retired, the village elders came to thank her, and one of them, a Hindu grandfather, said, “Sister, we never became like you in religion, but you have made our whole village more kind.” Some years later a few families asked a priest to teach them about Jesus. The sister heard the news in her convent in Kerala and said only, “The yeast takes its time.”

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you plant the kingdom like a mustard seed and hide it like yeast in the dough. As we gather in your name, make us small and faithful, and let your kingdom grow in us. Amen.
share: It is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs (Matthew 13:32). What small beginning is God asking of me?
Yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour (Matthew 13:33). Where am I called to be yeast in my workplace or neighbourhood?
If we judged ourselves, we would not be judged (1 Corinthians 11:31). How do I prepare myself before Holy Communion?
When you come together to eat, wait for one another (1 Corinthians 11:33). Who is left behind in our parish or family?
pm.resp: Lord, let your kingdom grow among us.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may grow like the mustard seed and shelter all peoples.
For missionaries and for small Christian communities in difficult places.
For Christians in public life and work, that they may be yeast for justice and kindness.
For the poor and those who are left out at our gatherings, that we may wait for them and serve them first.
For all who will receive Holy Communion this week, that they may prepare with humble hearts.
pm.close: Father, your kingdom grows from the smallest seed and works like hidden yeast. Make us faithful in small things, ready to receive your Son worthily, and attentive to one another. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews: God promises a new covenant: I will write my laws on their hearts, and remember their sins no more.
John: Jesus drives the merchants from the Temple: Stop making my Father's house a marketplace.
Jesus: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up; he spoke of the temple of his body.
2027-05-20.action: Ask the Holy Spirit today to write one commandment on your heart, and keep it gladly.
2027-05-20.question: What tables has greed or bargaining set up in the temple of my life?
catechism: The New Law, grace of the Spirit.
The Church, temple of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: St Bernardine of Siena

Bernardine was an Italian priest who walked from town to town preaching about Jesus. He carried a board with the letters IHS, the first letters of the name of Jesus in Greek, painted in gold with rays like the sun. He asked people to put the name of Jesus over their doors instead of signs of quarrels. The Latin Church remembers him on 20 May.
2027-05-20.special: First Thursday of the Apostles. Anniversary of the first Syro-Malabar Bishops' Synod (1993).
term: Synod

From the Greek for ‘walking together’: a gathering of bishops to pray, discern and decide for the life of the Church. In our Major Archiepiscopal Church the Synod of Bishops, with the Major Archbishop, is the highest governing body.

family.explain: When Jesus went to the Temple in Jerusalem, he found people buying and selling animals and changing money, making it noisy like a market. Jesus loved his Father's house, so he chased them out and said, ‘Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!’ Our church is God's house too, and so is our own heart, because the Holy Spirit lives there.
family.intention: We pray for our parish church and for everyone who keeps it clean and beautiful, and for our bishops.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we show that the church is God's house when we go there on Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

An elderly woman in a parish near Pala used to come every Saturday afternoon with a broom and a cloth to clean the church before Sunday. When a young man asked why she did it unpaid at her age, she said, ‘My husband built our house, and I kept it for fifty years. This is the Lord's house; while my hands can hold a broom, I will keep it for him.’ Then she added, smiling, ‘And while I sweep the floor, I ask him to sweep my heart.’ The young man came back the next Saturday with a mop.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, true Temple of God, gather us in your presence and fill us with your Holy Spirit, who writes your law on our hearts. Amen.
share: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts (Hebrews 8:10). Which of God's commands do I keep only from outside, without love?
Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace! (John 2:16). What needs to be driven out of my heart or my home?
Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up (John 2:19). How has the Risen Lord rebuilt something broken in my life?
He himself knew what was in everyone (John 2:25). Do I find comfort or fear in being fully known by Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, make us your living temple.
interc: For the Syro-Malabar Synod of Bishops and our Major Archbishop, that they may walk together in the Holy Spirit.
For our parish churches, that they may be true houses of prayer.
For the Jewish people, to whom the covenant was first given, that God may bless them in his faithfulness.
For all who have made money their god, that the Lord may overturn their tables and turn their hearts to love.
For our families, that the law of love may be written on every heart.
pm.close: Father, you made a new covenant in the Blood of your Son and sent your Spirit to write it on our hearts. Cleanse us, dwell in us and make us one temple of praise. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Isaiah: Strengthen the weak hands; the lame shall leap like a deer on the Holy Way.
Acts: I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.
Paul: without love I am nothing; faith, hope and love abide, and the greatest of these is love.
Luke: at Nain Jesus has compassion on a widow and raises her only son; the blind see and the lame walk.
2027-05-21.action: Give one person today something better than money: your time, your attention and a prayer in Jesus' Name.
2027-05-21.question: Who is lying at the gate of my life, waiting for me to look at them?
catechism: The apostles share Christ's healing ministry.
kidsaint: St Peter and St John at the Beautiful Gate
