Peter and John were two best friends among the apostles. One afternoon, on their way to pray, they met a man who had never been able to walk. He asked for money, but they had none. Peter said, ‘I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you,’ and in the name of Jesus he helped him stand. The man jumped and danced into the Temple, thanking God! That is one reason why this day is often called the Friday of Gold.
2027-05-21.special: The Friday of Gold: first Friday of the Apostles; the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate (Acts 3).
term: Friday of Gold

The first Friday after Pentecost in the Syriac Churches, recalling the first miracle of the apostles after the coming of the Spirit, the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate. Its name is commonly linked with Peter's words, “I have no silver or gold.” In Malayalam it is known as Swarnavelli.

family.explain: Peter and John were going to pray in the Temple. At the gate sat a man who had never walked; he begged for coins. Peter had no money, but he said, ‘What I have I give you: in the name of Jesus, stand up and walk!’ He took the man's hand, and the man jumped up and went into the Temple praising God. We may not have money to give, but we can always give love, kindness and the name of Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick or cannot walk, and for all who care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us give to someone this week that does not cost money?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Thrissur a group of young people noticed that an old man in a wheelchair always sat outside the church during the Qurbana, because there were steps and no one to lift him. One Sunday a college student asked him, ‘Appacha, shall we go in?’ With two friends he carried the chair up the steps. The old man wept through the whole Qurbana. The next month the youth group raised money for a ramp, and the student began to fetch him every Sunday. ‘We had no money at first,’ she said later, ‘but we had arms, and that was enough to begin.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in your holy Name the lame walk and the dead are raised. Gather us now, poor in gold and rich in your Spirit, and teach us the more excellent way of love. Amen.
share: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees (Isaiah 35:3). Whose weak hands can I strengthen this week?
I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you (Acts 3:6). What do I have that I could give in the name of Jesus?
Love is patient; love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4). Where am I most impatient or unkind?
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion for her (Luke 7:13). Whom has God placed before my eyes so that I might have compassion?
pm.resp: Lord, in your Name, raise us up.
interc: For the Church, that she may be poor in gold and rich in charity, and give the world the Name of Jesus.
For the disabled, the sick and the elderly, that our parishes may welcome them and help them enter God's house.
For the Jewish people, the descendants of Abraham, that they may receive the blessing promised to all the families of the earth.
For widows and mothers who mourn their children, that the Lord may say to them, Do not weep.
For ourselves, that the Holy Spirit may give us the greatest gift, which is love.
pm.close: Father, in the Name of your Son the apostles raised the lame man at the Beautiful Gate. By the Holy Spirit make us gentle and bold, to give what we have and to love without end. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: the body is one and has many members; so it is with Christ.
Paul: God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.
Jesus: work for the food that endures for eternal life; this is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.
2027-05-22.action: Offer one hour of hidden service to your parish this month.
2027-05-22.question: Do I seek Jesus for himself, or only for what he gives me?
kidsaint: St Rita of Cascia

Rita lived in Italy long ago. She was a wife and mother whose husband was hot-tempered; she prayed for him with great patience until he changed. After he died she became a nun. People call her the saint of impossible things, because she trusted God when everything seemed hopeless. The Latin Church remembers her on 22 May.
2027-05-22.special: First Saturday of the Apostles. Eve of the feast of the Most Holy Trinity.
term: Body of Christ

Paul's name for the Church: the faithful, joined by Baptism and the Eucharist to Christ their Head and to one another as members, each with a different gift from the one Spirit. The same words name the Holy Eucharist, the sacrament that makes the Church one Body.

family.explain: Our body has many parts: eyes to see, ears to hear, hands to work and feet to walk. Imagine if the foot said, ‘I am not a hand, so I am not part of the body!’ That would be silly. Paul says the Church is like a body, and Jesus is the head. In our family and our parish everyone has a different job, and all are needed.
family.intention: We pray for everyone in our parish, especially those whose work no one sees.
family.ask: Ask: “What is my job in our family and in our parish? How can I do it with love?”

illus: An illustration

At a parish feast in Kuttanad, a small boy of seven was upset because his older brother was carrying the processional cross and he was only allowed to fold chairs. His grandmother took him aside. ‘Monae, if no one folds the chairs, where will the people sit for the next feast? The cross goes ahead, the chairs come after, and the Lord sees both.’ That evening the boy folded more chairs than anyone, and the parish priest thanked him by name at the end of the Qurbana. Years later, as a young man, he still remembered it as the day he learned that the Church is a body.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Head of the Body, we are many, but we are one in you. Fill us with the Spirit we drank in Baptism, and make us one heart as we pray. Amen.
share: For just as the body is one and has many members… so it is with Christ (1 Corinthians 12:12). Do I see myself as a living member of Christ's Body?
God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose (1 Corinthians 12:18). Where has God placed me to serve?
You are looking for me… because you ate your fill of the loaves (John 6:26). Why do I seek Jesus?
This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent (John 6:29). How can I strengthen my faith this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one Body in you.
interc: For the unity of the Church, that all members may honour one another's gifts.
For those who feel useless or unwanted in the Church, that they may find their place in the Body.
For the hungry of the world, that they may receive bread, and for all of us, that we may hunger for the bread of eternal life.
For our parishes, that they may welcome every member, the strong and the weak.
Through the prayers of the Blessed Virgin Mary, for a deeper faith in our families.
pm.close: Father, by the one Spirit you made us one Body in your Son. Keep us united in faith and love, and feed us with the bread that endures for eternal life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: hold fast to what we have attained, and imitate those who live by the example of the apostles.
Paul: many live as enemies of the cross, but our citizenship is in heaven, and Christ will transform our lowly body.
Jesus to Martha: I am the resurrection and the life; Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe.
2027-05-24.action: Visit or call someone who is grieving, and pray with them for their beloved dead.
2027-05-24.question: Do I live as a citizen of heaven, or are my mind and heart set only on earthly things?
catechism: Jesus, the resurrection and the life.
kidsaint: St Martha of Bethany

Martha was a good friend of Jesus. She lived in Bethany with her sister Mary and her brother Lazarus, and she loved to cook for Jesus when he came to visit. When Lazarus died, Martha ran to meet Jesus, and Jesus told her, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ Martha said, ‘Yes, Lord, I believe!’ Then Jesus raised Lazarus from the tomb. The Church remembers her on 29 July.
2027-05-24.special: Second Monday of the Apostles. The day after the feast of the Most Holy Trinity.
term: Citizenship in heaven

Paul's image for the Christian's true belonging: as Philippi was a Roman colony whose people were citizens of Rome, so Christians live on earth as citizens of the kingdom of heaven, awaiting the Saviour and the resurrection of the body.

family.explain: Martha's brother Lazarus had died, and she was very sad. When Jesus came, she ran to meet him. Jesus told her, ‘I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live.’ Martha said, ‘Yes, Lord, I believe!’ Jesus is stronger than death. When someone we love dies, we can be sad, but we also have hope: Jesus will raise them up.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and relatives who have died, and for families who are sad today.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom do we miss who has gone to God? Let us say a prayer for them now.”

illus: An illustration

On the anniversary of her husband's death, an elderly widow in Kottayam walks every year to the parish cemetery with her grandchildren. She lights a small oil lamp on the grave, sprinkles holy water and prays aloud the words of Martha. One year her teenage grandson asked why she did not cry anymore. She said, ‘For the first years I cried at this grave. Now I come here to say I believe. Your appachan is not in this stone; he is with the One who said, I am the resurrection. I come to tell him I am still on the way.’ The boy said later that it was the first time he understood what Christians mean by hope.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, you met Martha on the road in her grief. Meet us now, and strengthen our faith in you. Amen.
share: Join in imitating me, and observe those who live according to the example you have in us (Philippians 3:17). Whose faith has shaped mine, and whom am I shaping?
Our citizenship is in heaven (Philippians 3:20). What earthly things have too great a hold on my heart?
Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died (John 11:21). What grief or disappointment do I need to bring honestly to Jesus?
I am the resurrection and the life… Do you believe this? (John 11:25–26). How would I answer Jesus today?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the resurrection and the life.
interc: For all who mourn, that the Risen Lord may meet them on the road as he met Martha.
For our beloved dead, that they may rise to the glory of Christ.
For those who live as enemies of the Cross, that they may be turned back with tears and love.
For parents, godparents and teachers, that their lives may be worth imitating.
For our parishes, that they may be communities of hope in time of death and sorrow.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and made him the resurrection and the life of all who believe. Strengthen our faith, comfort the sorrowing, and bring us with all our beloved dead to the glory of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? You are the seal of my apostleship.
Paul: we have not made use of this right, but we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel.
Jesus: Do you also wish to go away? Peter: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
2027-05-25.action: Make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament before Thursday's feast, and pray Peter's words there.
2027-05-25.question: When following Jesus is hard, do I walk away or say with Peter, Lord, to whom can I go?
catechism: Providing for the needs of the Church.
kidsaint: St Bede the Venerable

Bede was an English monk who lived more than twelve hundred years ago. He went to the monastery when he was seven and spent his whole life praying, singing the psalms, studying the Bible and writing books. He wrote the first history of the Church in England. On the day he died he was still translating the Gospel of John for his people. The Latin Church remembers him on 25 May.
2027-05-25.special: Second Tuesday of the Apostles. The Gospel closes the discourse on the Bread of Life, two days before the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ.
term: Apostle

From the Greek for ‘one who is sent’. The Twelve, and Paul, were apostles because the Risen Christ sent them; the bishops are their successors. Our Church is called apostolic because it was founded on the witness of Mar Thoma and keeps the faith of the apostles.

family.explain: Jesus told the people that he would give them his own Body to eat and his Blood to drink. Many found this too hard and went away. Jesus asked his twelve apostles, ‘Do you also wish to go away?’ Peter said, ‘Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.’ At Holy Qurbana Jesus really gives us himself. Even when we do not understand everything, we stay with Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for people who have stopped coming to church, that they may come back to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do this week to prepare for the feast of the Body and Blood of Jesus on Thursday?”

illus: An illustration

A religious sister from Thrissur has worked for twenty years in a mission station in Madhya Pradesh. When she first arrived she had a salary of almost nothing, no vehicle and no electricity in the convent. Her family asked her to come home and teach in a good school in Kerala, where she could live in comfort. She wrote back: ‘I have every right to come home. But if I leave, who will teach these children to pray? Here I have learned what Paul meant: I would rather bear anything than be an obstacle to the Gospel.’ Today three of the children she taught are catechists in their own villages.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you have the words of eternal life. We gather to listen to you; keep us faithful when your word is hard. Amen.
share: Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? (1 Corinthians 9:1). Where have I met the Risen Lord, and to whom does he send me?
We endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ (1 Corinthians 9:12). What right could I lay aside so that others may see Christ?
Do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). When have I been tempted to walk away from Jesus?
Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life (John 6:68). How has Jesus kept me close in a hard time?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of eternal life.
interc: For the bishops, priests and missionaries of our Church, that they may proclaim the Gospel without obstacle.
For those who have walked away from the Church because a teaching was hard, that they may hear the Lord's question and return.
For a deeper faith in the true presence of Christ in the Holy Qurbana as we prepare for Thursday's feast.
For generous hearts in our parishes, to support the Church and the poor.
For ourselves, that we may never betray the Lord who chose us.
pm.close: Father, your Son gives us his Body and Blood, the bread of eternal life. Keep us faithful to him when his word is hard, and make us generous servants of his Gospel. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus: anyone who comes to me I will never drive away; I will raise them up on the last day.
No one comes to Jesus unless the Father draws them: faith is a gift.
Paul: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; you were bought with a price, so glorify God in your body.
2027-05-26.action: Make one concrete choice today to honour your body as the Spirit's temple, and go to confession soon if you have stayed away.
2027-05-26.question: Have I let familiarity hide Jesus from me?

family.explain: Jesus says that he will never send away anyone who comes to him. Even when we have done something wrong, we can always go back to him. Saint Paul says our body is like a church where the Holy Spirit lives. That is why we take care of our bodies: we wash, we eat good food, we sleep, and we never hurt our own body or anyone else's.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick, old or disabled, and for those who care for their bodies with love.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way our family can take better care of the bodies God gave us?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Kottayam worked in a care home in Ireland where many of the residents had no visitors. A younger colleague noticed how slowly and gently she washed and dressed the old people, especially the ones who could no longer speak. ‘Why do you take so much trouble?’ she asked. ‘Nobody is watching.’ The nurse said that her grandmother had washed her grandfather's body every day during his last illness and used to say, ‘This is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and one day it will rise.’ ‘So I am not just washing a body,’ she said. ‘I am cleaning a temple.’ Some weeks later the colleague asked if she could come with her to Sunday Mass.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you never drive away anyone who comes to you. We come to you now; draw us closer by your Father's love and fill us with your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away (John 6:37). When have I been afraid to come back to the Lord?
Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph? (John 6:42). Has familiarity made me deaf to Jesus?
No one can come to me unless drawn by the Father (John 6:44). For whom do I pray, that the Father may draw them?
Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 6:19). How do I treat this temple?
pm.resp: Lord, draw us to yourself.
interc: For the Church in this Season of the Apostles, that she may welcome every person who comes, as Jesus does.
For young people tempted to treat their bodies as things to be used, that they may discover their dignity as temples of the Spirit.
For those who are slaves to drink, drugs or pornography, that they may find healing and strength.
For nurses, doctors and all who care for the sick and the old, that they may serve with reverence.
For our dead, that the Lord may raise them up on the last day.
pm.close: Father, you give to your Son all who come to him, and he loses none of them. Draw us by your grace, keep our bodies holy for your Spirit, and raise us with Christ on the last day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Genesis: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram.
Malachi: God rejects careless worship and promises a pure offering among the nations from the rising of the sun to its setting.
Paul: I received from the Lord what I handed on to you: This is my body that is for you; examine yourselves before you eat.
John: my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink; whoever eats me abides in me and will live forever.
2027-05-27.action: Spend fifteen minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, and examine your conscience before your next Communion.
2027-05-27.question: Do I come to the Holy Qurbana as to the true Body and Blood of the Lord?
catechism: Melchizedek and the bread and wine.
kidsaint: St Carlo Acutis

Carlo was an Italian boy who loved computers, football and his dog. Most of all he loved Jesus in the Holy Qurbana. He went to Mass every day he could, and he made a website about Eucharistic miracles from around the world. He used to say that the Eucharist was his highway to heaven. Carlo died of leukaemia in 2006 when he was fifteen, and Pope Leo XIV declared him a saint in 2025. Lesson: you are never too young to love Jesus in the Eucharist!
2027-05-27.special: Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ (Syro-Malabar, Thursday). Latin Church in India: Corpus Christi on Sunday 30 May.
term: Qurbana

The Syriac word for offering or sacrifice, used by the Syro-Malabar Church for the Eucharistic celebration, the Holy Qurbana. The solemn form celebrated on great occasions is called Raza, the Mystery. The word says what the Church believes: the Qurbana is the sacrifice of Christ made present, and the Body and Blood of the Lord given to the faithful.

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus had supper with his friends. He took bread and said, “This is my body that is for you.” He took the cup and said, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.” Every time the priest says these words at the Holy Qurbana, the bread and wine become Jesus himself. It still looks like bread, but it is Jesus. That is why we kneel, we are quiet, and we receive him with clean hearts.
family.intention: We pray for children preparing for their First Holy Communion, and for those who are sick and cannot come to church.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we get ready at home on Saturday for the Holy Qurbana on Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in a village near Changanassery could no longer walk to church after a stroke. Every Sunday a young deacon brought Holy Communion to her house. Her grandson, who had stopped going to church, noticed that every Saturday evening his grandmother asked him to sweep the front room, put a white cloth on the small table, place a candle and a crucifix on it, and help her into a clean sari. One Saturday he asked her, a little impatiently, why she made such a fuss for a few minutes' visit. She said, ‘Because the King is coming to my house.’ The next morning, when the deacon arrived, the grandson found that he was kneeling beside her without having planned to. ‘I had heard the word Real Presence a hundred times in catechism,’ he said later. ‘I understood it in my grandmother's front room.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, truly present in the Holy Qurbana, we adore you and we thank you. Gather us now around your word and make our hearts ready to receive you. Amen.
share: Melchizedek brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High (Genesis 14:18). What does it mean to me that Christ is a priest forever?
By thinking that the Lord's table may be despised (Malachi 1:7). Have I given God only my leftovers?
Examine yourselves, and only then eat of the bread (1 Corinthians 11:28). How do I prepare for Holy Communion?
Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them (John 6:56). Where do I carry the Lord after I receive him?
pm.resp: Lord, you are the living bread: give us life.
interc: For the Church, that she may always draw her life from the Eucharist and offer the pure offering in every place.
For our priests, that they may celebrate the Holy Qurbana with faith and reverence.
For children preparing for First Holy Communion and for their families.
For the sick and the housebound, that they may receive the Lord in their homes.
For the hungry of the world, that those who share the one bread may share their bread with the poor.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave us his Body and Blood as true food and true drink. Make us discern his Body in the sacrament and in our neighbour, abide in him always, and come at last to the banquet of heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus: they shall all be taught by God; everyone who has learned from the Father comes to me.
Jesus is the bread of life: the manna fed bodies that died; whoever eats this bread will not die.
Paul: the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God; all things are yours, and you belong to Christ.
2027-05-28.action: Read next Sunday's Gospel at home before the Qurbana, and make peace with someone you have quarrelled with over a preacher or a parish matter.
2027-05-28.question: Do I let God teach me, or do I measure the things of God by the wisdom of the world?

family.explain: When the people of Israel walked through the desert, God fed them every morning with manna, a special bread from heaven. But one day they all died. Jesus says that he is a better bread: the bread of life. When we believe in him and receive him in the Holy Qurbana, he gives us a life that never ends, even after we die.
family.intention: We pray for teachers, catechists and all who teach children about God.
family.ask: Ask: “What did God teach us this week through the Bible or through someone?”

illus: An illustration

A professor of physics at a university in Kerala used to stay behind after Sunday Qurbana to help with the catechism class for six-year-olds. His colleagues teased him: a scientist teaching nursery prayers. One day a student asked him why he bothered. He said that in his laboratory he had learned how much he did not know, and in the catechism room he had learned to be taught. ‘The children ask the real questions,’ he said. ‘Who made God? Where is Grandmother now? Is Jesus really in the Host? I have to go home and pray before I can answer them. In the lab I am the teacher. On Sunday mornings God teaches me through them.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the bread of life, and you teach us the ways of the Father. Open our ears and our hearts as we gather around your word. Amen.
share: They shall all be taught by God (John 6:45). Through whom has God been teaching me lately?
I am the bread of life (John 6:48). How hungry am I for Jesus in the Holy Qurbana?
The wisdom of this world is foolishness with God (1 Corinthians 3:19). Where have I trusted worldly wisdom more than God's word?
All things are yours, and you belong to Christ (1 Corinthians 3:21, 23). Do I live as one who belongs to Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, bread of life, teach us and feed us.
interc: For the Church, that in this Season of the Apostles she may teach the nations as one taught by God.
For catechists, teachers and parents, that they may pass on the faith with wisdom and love.
For students preparing for examinations and choosing their studies, that they may seek true wisdom.
For parishes and communities divided over leaders and movements, that they may find unity in Christ.
For the dying, that the bread of life may carry them through death to eternal life.
pm.close: Father, you teach all your children and draw them to your Son. Make us humble enough to learn, hungry enough to receive the bread of life, and faithful enough to belong to Christ in everything. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: A boy gives five barley loaves and two fish; Jesus gives thanks and feeds five thousand.
Gather up the fragments so that nothing may be lost: twelve baskets are left over; Jesus refuses to be made a king of bread.
Paul: the cup of blessing and the bread we break are a sharing in the blood and body of Christ; one bread, one body.
2027-05-29.action: Waste no food this week, and share what is left over with someone in need.
2027-05-29.question: What small gift am I holding back because I think it is not enough?

family.explain: Thousands of hungry people followed Jesus. A boy had five small loaves and two fish, and he gave them to Jesus. Jesus thanked God, and everyone ate until they were full! Then Jesus said, “Gather up what is left over, so that nothing is wasted,” and there were twelve baskets full. Jesus can do great things with the little we give him.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough to eat today.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us give to Jesus this week, even if it seems small?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Thrissur the youth group noticed how much food was thrown away after big weddings and feasts. They made an arrangement with three auditoriums: when a function ended, the manager would call them. Within an hour, a group of young people with clean containers would collect the untouched food and take it to an old-age home, a hostel for migrant workers and two families in the parish who were struggling. The first time they went, one boy grumbled that it was beneath him to carry leftovers. On the way back he said quietly, ‘Now I understand why Jesus told the disciples to gather up the fragments.’ The group named their work ‘Twelve Baskets’.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you fed the hungry crowd with five barley loaves. Take the little we bring tonight and bless it, and make us one body in you. Amen.
share: There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish (John 6:9). What small gift do I have to offer?
Gather up the fragments left over, so that nothing may be lost (John 6:12). What or whom am I wasting or neglecting?
The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ? (1 Corinthians 10:16). How does Communion make me one with others?
Flee from the worship of idols (1 Corinthians 10:14). What has taken God's place in my heart?
pm.resp: Lord, bread of life, make us one.
interc: For the Church, that the one bread may make her one body, healed of every division.
For the hungry and the poor, that those who share the Eucharist may share their bread.
For families who waste and families who want, that God may teach us to gather the fragments.
For those who trust in charms and lucky days instead of God, that they may find peace in the Lord.
Through the intercession of the Mother of God, for all who have prayed the devotions of the month of May.
pm.close: Father, your Son took the little that was offered and fed a multitude. Bless our small gifts, keep our hearts from idols, and make us who share the one bread one body in Christ, caring for the least of our brothers and sisters. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mary sets out in haste to the hill country to visit Elizabeth.
At her greeting John leaps in the womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Spirit, calls her the mother of my Lord.
Elizabeth: blessed is she who believed; Paul: let love be genuine, rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep.
2027-05-31.action: Visit someone this week who needs you, and do not postpone it.
2027-05-31.question: Whom is the Lord asking me to visit in haste?
catechism: Mother of my Lord: the Theotokos.
kidsaint: St Elizabeth

Elizabeth and her husband Zechariah were old and had no children. God gave them a baby, John. When Mary came to visit, baby John jumped for joy inside Elizabeth! Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit and said, “Blessed are you among women!” We say her words every time we pray the Hail Mary. Lesson: when Jesus comes close, our hearts can jump for joy too!
2027-05-31.special: Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary (important Marian feast). Close of the month of Mary.
term: Magnificat

The song of Mary in Luke 1:46–55, named from its first word in Latin: My soul magnifies the Lord. Mary sings it in the house of Elizabeth. The Church prays it every day, and it echoes the song of Hannah and the psalms of Israel: God lifts up the lowly and fills the hungry with good things.

family.explain: After the angel visited Mary, she heard that her cousin Elizabeth was going to have a baby in her old age. Mary hurried to help her, walking over the hills. When Mary said hello, Elizabeth's baby jumped for joy, because Jesus was inside Mary! Elizabeth said, “Blessed are you among women.” Mary stayed three months to help. We too can go quickly to help people in our family who need us.
family.intention: We pray for mothers who are expecting babies, and for grandparents and old people who need our help.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can our family visit or help this week, like Mary helped Elizabeth?”

illus: An illustration

A young woman from a village near Kottayam, expecting her first child, was living with her husband in Bengaluru when the doctor told her she must rest completely for the last three months. Her own mother had died years before. One evening her father's sister, a widow in her sixties from the hills of Idukki, rang to say she was coming. She arrived two days later after an overnight bus journey, with a cloth bag of jackfruit chips and a rosary, and stayed until the baby was baptised. She cooked, prayed the Rosary every evening at the young woman's bedside, and told stories of the family. Years later, when a neighbour in her building was in the same situation, the young mother went down every day to help. ‘My aunt never preached to me,’ she said. ‘She just came quickly, and stayed.’

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who filled Elizabeth at Mary's greeting, fill us now. With Mary, the Mother of our Lord, we gather to listen and to praise. Amen.
share: Mary set out and went with haste (Luke 1:39). What visit have I been postponing?
The child leaped in her womb (Luke 1:41). When has the nearness of Jesus filled me with joy?
Why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me? (Luke 1:43). How do I welcome Mary and Jesus into my home?
Blessed is she who believed (Luke 1:45). Which word of God do I find hard to believe?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may go out in haste to carry Christ to all.
For expectant mothers and their unborn children, that they may be protected and welcomed with joy.
For the elderly and those who care for them, that no one may be left alone.
For families who prayed together in the month of Mary, that their prayer may continue through the year.
For all who doubt God's promises, that they may believe like Mary.
pm.close: Father, you made the Blessed Virgin Mary the dwelling of your Son and sent her in haste to serve. Through her intercession, give us faith in your word, joy in Christ's presence and genuine love for our neighbour. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, this is the last Sunday before the Ascension. On Thursday we will celebrate the Lord going up to heaven. Today's readings are like a farewell and a sending.

Isaiah sings: “How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace” (Isaiah 52:7). The apostles were such messengers; Mar Thoma brought the good news to our land. Now our feet are called to carry it.

In Acts, Peter sees a vision and hears: “What God has made clean, you must not call profane” (Acts 10:15). God was teaching him that the Gospel is for every nation. Soon Peter entered the house of a Roman officer, Cornelius, and baptised his family.

Paul tells the Ephesians that Christ “is our peace” and “has broken down the dividing wall” (Ephesians 2:14). In Christ there are no strangers. We too have walls: caste, money, language, old quarrels. Christ has broken them down. Let us not build them again.

In the Gospel Jesus prays for us: “that they may all be one... so that the world may believe that you have sent me” (John 17:21). When Christians are divided, people find it hard to believe. When we love one another, the world sees Jesus.
So this week, let us pray for unity, make peace with one person, and prepare to celebrate the Ascension on Thursday. The Lord wants us to be with him where he is. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus prayed for you! He asked his Father that all his friends would be one big family.
When you share, forgive and play kindly with others, you help Jesus' prayer come true.

homily: Dear friends, forty days after Easter Jesus went up to heaven. Today we celebrate his Ascension, a great Feast of our Lord and a day of obligation.

In the first reading Elijah is taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire. His disciple Elisha would not leave him, and asked for “a double share of your spirit” (2 Kings 2:9). Because Elisha saw his master go, he received his spirit and his mantle. The apostles saw Jesus go up, and ten days later they received the Holy Spirit.

In Acts the apostles ask about the kingdom. Jesus answers, “you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses... to the ends of the earth” (Acts 1:8). Then a cloud took him out of their sight, and two angels said, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” (Acts 1:11). The Ascension does not tell us to stare at the sky. It sends us to be witnesses.

Paul tells Timothy that there is “one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human” (1 Timothy 2:5). A man, our brother, is now at the right hand of the Father, praying for us. That is why we pray for everyone, for rulers, for the sick, for the whole world.

In the Gospel Jesus lifts up his hands and blesses his disciples, and while he is blessing them he is carried up into heaven. And they go back “with great joy” (Luke 24:52). His blessing remains over us.
From tomorrow, with Mary and the apostles, we wait and pray for the Holy Spirit. Let us begin a novena in our homes. Christ has gone ahead to prepare a place for us. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus went up to heaven! Before he went, he lifted up his hands and blessed his friends.
He is with his Father, but he is still with us. He promised to send the Holy Spirit. Let us pray with Mary: Come, Holy Spirit!

opts.a: Our nature at the right hand of the Father
intro: The Ascension is not Jesus leaving his humanity behind. He takes it with him. Where the Head has gone, the body hopes to follow.

points.h: One like a son of man
sub: A great high priest who knows our weakness.
points.apply: Approach the throne of grace with confidence in prayer today.

points.h: I go to prepare a place for you
sub: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD?
points.apply: Think about heaven for a few minutes each day this week.

points.h: Seek the things that are above
sub: Set your minds on things above.
Lifting up our hearts at the Qurbana.
points.apply: Give one earthly worry to God each day, and lift up your heart.

concl: In Christ, our human nature has entered heaven.
We live on earth with our hearts where Christ is.
opts.resolve: This week I will lift up my heart each day to Christ at the Father's right hand and give him one worry.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate the Ascension of our Lord. Forty days after Easter, while he was blessing his disciples, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven (Luke 24:51). But he did not leave behind the body that was born of Mary and nailed to the Cross. He took our human nature with him into heaven.

Daniel saw in vision one like a human being coming with the clouds of heaven, and to him was given dominion and glory (Daniel 7:13–14). That is the Ascension. A man, our brother, now sits at the right hand of the Father. Hebrews says: we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:15–16).

The Psalm asks: who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? Lift up your heads, O gates, that the King of glory may come in (Psalm 24:3, 7). Christ has gone in, and he said: in my Father's house there are many dwelling places. I go to prepare a place for you (John 14:2). Heaven is not a dream. It is our home, and the door has been opened by one of us.

So Paul tells us: if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God (Colossians 3:1). That does not mean neglecting the earth. It means living here with our hearts set there. In every Holy Qurbana the priest invites us to lift up our minds on high. Let us really lift them up.

This week let us think a little each day about heaven, our true home. Let us give one worry each day to the Lord at the Father's right hand. And let us live on earth as people whose Head is already in glory. Alleluia! Amen.

intro: Before he ascended, Jesus opened the disciples' minds to understand the Scriptures and sent them to preach repentance to all nations. Then they returned to Jerusalem with great joy.

sub: Moses, the prophets and the psalms.
Ezra reading the law to the people.
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the day each morning until Pentecost.

points.h: Repentance and forgiveness to all nations
points.apply: Invite one person back to confession or to the Qurbana.

points.h: Continually in the temple blessing God
sub: God has gone up with a shout.
Praise while waiting for the Spirit.
points.apply: Pray the novena to the Holy Spirit with your family until Pentecost.

concl: The ascended Lord leaves us his word, his mission and his joy.
We wait for the Spirit by reading, witnessing and praising.
opts.resolve: Until Pentecost I will read the daily Gospel and pray the novena to the Holy Spirit with my family.
homily: Dear friends, Luke tells us what Jesus did just before his Ascension. He said: everything written about me in the law of Moses, the prophets, and the psalms must be fulfilled. Then he opened their minds to understand the scriptures (Luke 24:44–45).

Long ago, when Ezra read the book of the law to the people, the Levites gave the sense, so that the people understood the reading (Nehemiah 8:8). Now the risen Lord himself gives the sense of the whole Bible: it speaks of him. Until Pentecost, let us read the Gospel of the day each morning, and ask him to open our minds too.

Then he said: repentance and forgiveness of sins is to be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. You are witnesses of these things (Luke 24:47–48). Jonah preached unwillingly, and yet the people of Nineveh believed God (Jonah 3:5). The apostles would preach willingly, and the Gospel would reach the ends of the earth, even our own Kerala through Mar Thoma.

Finally, while he was blessing them, he was carried up into heaven. And they worshiped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy; and they were continually in the temple blessing God (Luke 24:52–53). The Psalm sings: God has gone up with a shout; sing praises to our King (Psalm 47:5–6). They were not sad. They knew he had not abandoned them, and they waited in praise.

So in these days before Pentecost let us read his word, invite one person back to confession or to the Holy Qurbana, and gather our families for the novena to the Holy Spirit. Let us wait as the apostles waited, with Mary, in joy and in prayer. Alleluia! Amen.

Dear friends, on Thursday we celebrated the Ascension, and next Sunday we will celebrate Pentecost. Today we stand in between, and the readings tell us one thing: the Lord who reigns in glory sends his people out.

Isaiah sees the Lord on a high throne, and the angels singing, “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts.” We sing that same hymn at every Holy Qurbana. Isaiah is afraid: “Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips.” An angel touches his lips with a burning coal from the altar, and his sin is taken away. Our Syriac Fathers saw in that coal a picture of the Holy Qurbana, placed on our lips. Then God asks, “Whom shall I send?” And Isaiah answers, “Here am I; send me!”

In Acts, the apostles are praying with Mary, the mother of Jesus. Judas is gone, and the circle of the Twelve must be complete before the Spirit comes. They choose a witness to the Resurrection. They do not make speeches; they pray: “Lord, you know everyone's heart.” Matthias is chosen. The work of the apostles is handed on. Our bishops stand in that line today. Let us pray for them.

Paul sings of Jesus, who “emptied himself, taking the form of a slave”, and went down to the Cross. “Therefore God also highly exalted him.” The Ascension is that exaltation. But Paul says: let the same mind be in you. Do nothing from selfish ambition. Regard others as better than yourselves. The Church goes up the way Christ went: by going down in humility and service.

In the Gospel the Risen Lord scolds his disciples for their unbelief, and then he sends these same weak men: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.” He is taken up into heaven, and “they went out and proclaimed the good news everywhere, while the Lord worked with them.” He is in heaven and at work on earth at the same time.

Thomas was one of those eleven. Because he went, we are here. Now the Lord asks each of us: Whom shall I send? Maybe across the sea, maybe across the road to a neighbour. Let us answer with Isaiah: Here am I; send me. And let us pray with Mary this week for the Holy Spirit, who will give us the strength to go. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Isaiah heard God ask, “Whom shall I send?” and he said, “Here am I; send me!”

Before Jesus went up to heaven, he sent his friends to tell everyone about him. Jesus wants you to be his helper too. This week, can you tell one friend something good about Jesus? Say to him: ‘Here I am, Jesus!’

homily: Dear friends, today is Pentecost, the fiftieth day, the Feast of Our Lord that crowns the Season of the Resurrection and opens the Season of the Apostles. Pentecost was already a Jewish feast, the harvest festival, linked by tradition with the giving of the Law on Sinai. So our first reading takes us to Sinai, where God told Israel: “you shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation” (Exodus 19:6).

At Sinai God came in cloud and fire and gave his Law on stone. In the upper room he comes in wind and fire and writes his law of love on hearts. “All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit” (Acts 2:4). A tongue of fire rested on each one. Mary was there with them. The Spirit who formed Christ in her womb now forms his Body, the Church.

The first thing the Spirit does is make the apostles speak. Frightened men go out into the street. And people from many nations hear them each “in the native language of each” (Acts 2:6): Parthians, Medes, Elamites and residents of Mesopotamia. Those are the lands of the Church of the East, from which our own liturgy and our Syriac heritage came. Babel scattered the peoples; Pentecost gathers them into one Church with many tongues.

Paul says: “no one can say ‘Jesus is Lord’ except by the Holy Spirit” (1 Corinthians 12:3). There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit, and each gift is given “for the common good” (12:7). No one in this church today is without a gift. We received the Spirit's seal in our Baptism and Thailabhishekam. The question is whether we use our gift for others.

Jesus told the sad disciples: “it is to your advantage that I go away” (John 16:7). He went to the Father so that the Advocate could come. “When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth” (16:13). The Spirit takes what belongs to Christ and gives it to us; and next Sunday we shall celebrate the Holy Trinity whom he reveals.

Today the Season of the Apostles begins. The Spirit who sent the apostles to the ends of the earth brought Mar Thoma to our shores. Let us not keep the fire to ourselves. Let us say every day, Come, Holy Spirit, and let us go out, each with our gift, to tell the world that Jesus is Lord. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, on Pentecost the Holy Spirit came like a strong wind and like little flames of fire on Jesus' friends and on Mother Mary. Then they were not afraid any more!
You received the Holy Spirit when you were baptised. Today, say this little prayer: “Come, Holy Spirit, make me brave and kind.”

opts.a: The Advocate who convicts and consoles
intro: Jesus calls the Holy Spirit the Advocate. He is the defender who stands beside us, and also the one who shows the world the truth about sin, righteousness and judgment.

points.h: It is to your advantage that I go
sub: The Spirit of wisdom and understanding.
points.apply: Pray each morning: Come, Holy Spirit, stand beside me today.

points.h: He will prove the world wrong about sin
sub: The Spirit shows us our sin.
Not to condemn, but to heal.
Receive the Holy Spirit; forgive sins.
points.apply: Make a good confession in this Season of the Apostles.

sub: A Spirit-filled life makes Christ known.
points.apply: Ask the Spirit to help you speak of Christ to one person this week.

concl: The Spirit stands beside us, convicts us of sin and glorifies Christ.
Pentecost is the gift of a Defender who never leaves us.
opts.resolve: In this Season of the Apostles I will make a good confession and pray daily for the Spirit's help.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the night before he died Jesus saw that his disciples were full of sorrow. He told them: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you (John 16:7). Today, at Pentecost, the Advocate has come.

The word Advocate means one who is called to stand beside you, a defender, a counsellor. Isaiah foretold that the spirit of the LORD would rest on the Messiah: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might (Isaiah 11:2). That same Spirit is now given to the Church and to each of us. We are never alone.

But Jesus also said: when he comes, he will prove the world wrong about sin and righteousness and judgment (John 16:8). The Spirit shows us our sin, not to crush us but to heal us. On Easter evening the risen Lord breathed on the apostles and said: receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them (John 20:22–23). Every confession is a little Pentecost. God promised through Ezekiel: a new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you (Ezekiel 36:26).

And Jesus said of the Spirit: he will glorify me, because he will take what is mine and declare it to you (John 16:14). The Spirit does not draw attention to himself. He makes Jesus known. Joel had promised: I will pour out my spirit on all flesh (Joel 2:28). Today that promise is kept, and every baptised person is called to make Christ known.

So let us pray each morning: Come, Holy Spirit, stand beside me today. Let us make a good confession in this Season of the Apostles. And let us ask the Spirit to give us the courage to speak of Christ, and to receive him with burning hearts at the Holy Qurbana. Alleluia! Amen.

opts.a: Mary in the upper room, and the Spirit at our altar
intro: Before Pentecost the disciples were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with Mary, the mother of Jesus. The Spirit came on a praying Church, and he still comes on every altar.

sub: How good when kindred live together.
The Spirit comes to a united Church.
points.apply: Make peace with someone in your parish or family before next Sunday.

sub: The Spirit came upon her at Nazareth.
Now she prays with the apostles.
points.apply: Pray the Rosary this week asking Mary to obtain the Spirit for your family.

sub: The Spirit is invoked in every Qurbana.
points.apply: At the next Qurbana, pay attention to the prayer calling down the Holy Spirit.

concl: The Spirit came upon a Church united in prayer with Mary.
He still descends at every Qurbana to make the gifts holy and to make us one.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray with Mary for the Spirit and make peace with someone before next Sunday.
homily: Dear friends, before the great day of Pentecost, the apostles did not organise a campaign. They prayed. Luke says: all these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14). And when the day came, they were all together in one place (Acts 2:1).

The Psalm says: how very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity (Psalm 133:1). The Spirit came upon a Church that was united and praying. If our families and parishes want the fire of the Spirit, we must first be together, forgiving one another and praying with one heart.

Mary was there. Long before the apostles, the Spirit had come upon her. At Nazareth the angel had said to her: the Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you (Luke 1:35). The Spirit who formed Christ in her womb now forms the Body of Christ, the Church. That is why we call her Mother of the Church. Where Mary prays, the Spirit is near.

At Mount Carmel, when Elijah prayed, the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the offering (1 Kings 18:38). Paul speaks of an offering made acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit (Romans 15:16). In every Holy Qurbana our Church calls upon the Holy Spirit to come down upon the bread and wine. The fire of Pentecost falls again on our altar, the gifts become the Body and Blood of Christ, and we who receive them are made one.

So in this Season of the Apostles let us make peace with someone before next Sunday. Let us pray the Rosary, asking Mary to obtain the Spirit for our families. And at the next Holy Qurbana, when the Spirit is invoked, let us bow our hearts and say: Come, Holy Spirit. Alleluia! Amen.
Dear friends, today, the Second Sunday of the Apostles, our Church celebrates the feast of the Most Holy Trinity: one God, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

We meet this mystery every day. We were baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. We make the sign of the Cross in that Name. Every Holy Qurbana begins and ends with the glory of the Three.

In Genesis the Lord appears to Abraham at Mamre as three visitors. Abraham runs to meet them, washes their feet and serves them a meal. The Fathers of the Church saw in this scene a sign of the Trinity. God comes to us as a guest, and we meet him when we welcome others.

Isaiah hears God say, “I am the first, and I am the last,” and, “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your own good, who leads you in the way you should go.” God is not far away; he leads us on our road.

Paul shows the Three at work in us: we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, and “God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit.” Even our sufferings, Paul says, can produce hope.

Jesus says that the Spirit will take what is his and give it to us, and “All that the Father has is mine.” The Father gives all to the Son, the Spirit shares it with us. That is the life of God, and we are invited into it. Let us live today as children of the Father, brothers and sisters of the Son, temples of the Holy Spirit. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, God is one, but God is three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. That is a big mystery, bigger than the sky! Even grown-ups cannot understand it fully.

But you can pray to the Holy Trinity every day. Make the sign of the Cross slowly: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. Each time, you are saying: I belong to God's family!

intro: We were baptised not into three names but into the one Name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Our whole Christian life is lived inside that Name.

points.apply: Bless your children each night with the sign of the cross.

sub: Hear, O Israel: the LORD is one.
One God the Father, one Lord Jesus Christ.
Not three gods, but one God in three Persons.
points.apply: Pray the Creed slowly once this week, phrase by phrase.
Sing or say the Holy, holy, holy at the Qurbana with full attention.

concl: We live within the Name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
Our faith is in one God, whom heaven and earth adore.
opts.resolve: This week I will bless my children each night and pray the Creed slowly once.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate the Most Holy Trinity. When we were baptised, the priest did not say: in the names. He said: in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit (Matthew 28:19). One Name, three Persons. Our whole life as Christians is lived inside that Name.

God told Moses to bless the people with the words: the LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace. Then he added: so they shall put my name on the Israelites, and I will bless them (Numbers 6:24–27). In Baptism God's Name was placed upon us. When parents sign their children with the cross at night, they put that Name on them again.

Israel's great prayer says: hear, O Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD alone (Deuteronomy 6:4). We Christians do not believe in three gods. Paul says: for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things (1 Corinthians 8:6). And the Spirit is the Lord, the giver of life. One God in three Persons, equal in glory, one in being.

Isaiah saw the Lord on his throne, and the seraphs called to one another: holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts (Isaiah 6:3). John heard the same song in heaven (Revelation 4:8). In every Holy Qurbana we join that song. We do not fully understand the Trinity; we adore.

So this week let us bless our children each night with the sign of the cross. Let us pray the Creed slowly, phrase by phrase. And at the Holy Qurbana let us sing the Holy, holy, holy with full hearts, as people who bear the Name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Amen.

opts.a: A hope that does not disappoint
intro: Paul's words in today's Epistle were written for people who suffer. The Father gives peace through the Son, and the Spirit pours love into our hearts, so that even suffering can become hope.

sub: Peace through our Lord Jesus Christ.
The effect of righteousness will be peace.
points.apply: Make your peace with God in confession if you have been away.
Offer one present suffering to God with trust.

sub: Those who wait for the Lord shall not be put to shame.
The Spirit has been given to us.
Hope rests on love already received.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who is suffering and bring them hope.

concl: The Trinity is not a distant puzzle but the God who holds us in suffering.
Father, Son and Spirit turn our trials into hope.
opts.resolve: This week I will offer one suffering to God and bring hope to someone who is suffering.
homily: Dear friends, today's feast can seem like a difficult doctrine for theologians. But listen to how Paul speaks of the Trinity in today's Epistle. He is not writing a textbook. He is writing to people who suffer.

He begins: since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). The Father is not our enemy. Through his Son he has made peace with us. Isaiah said: the effect of righteousness will be peace (Isaiah 32:17). If we have been far from God, the door of confession is open.

Then Paul says something surprising: we also boast in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope (Romans 5:3–4). Job, in his pain, said: when he has tested me, I shall come out like gold (Job 23:10). Suffering in itself is not good. But in God's hands it can shape us, like gold in the fire.

And hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us (Romans 5:5). God promised through Isaiah: those who wait for me shall not be put to shame (Isaiah 49:23). Our hope is not wishful thinking. It rests on the love of the Father, shown in the Son, and poured into us by the Spirit.

So the Trinity is not far from our kitchens and hospital beds. The Father holds us, the Son walks with us, the Spirit comforts us. Let us offer one suffering to God this week with trust, and let us bring hope to someone who is suffering, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

Dear friends, two weeks after Pentecost, the readings show us a Church on the move. At Mount Horeb God said to his people, “You have stayed long enough at this mountain. Resume your journey” (Deuteronomy 1:6–7). The apostles did not stay in the Upper Room; the Spirit sent them out, and Mar Thoma came even to our shores.

We too can settle on our own mountain: our group, our habits, our comfort. The Lord says to us: you have stayed long enough. Go out to the family you do not know, to the parishioner who has stopped coming, to those who have never heard of Christ.

Isaiah weeps over a people who forgot God: “The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s crib; but Israel does not know” (Isaiah 1:3). A farm animal knows who feeds it. Do we remember the One who feeds us every day? Let our homes show to whom they belong.

Saint Paul speaks to married couples: husband and wife belong to each other, and should give themselves to each other with love; they may pray together and support each other. And he says, each has a particular gift from God (1 Corinthians 7:7). Marriage is a gift; the life of priests and sisters is a gift. Let us honour both and pray for both.

In the Gospel a man lies wounded on the road. A priest and a Levite pass by. A Samaritan, the one the listeners least expected, stops, binds his wounds, pours in oil and wine, and takes him to an inn. Jesus asks: who was a neighbour? “The one who showed him mercy.” “Go and do likewise” (Luke 10:37).

The Fathers saw in the Samaritan Jesus himself, who stopped for us, healed us with the sacraments and brought us to the inn of the Church. Healed by him, we cannot pass by on the other side. Let us become neighbours to the injured, the migrant, the lonely and the stranger, whatever their caste or religion. Amen.
kids: Children, a man was hurt on the road. Two people walked past without helping. But a Samaritan stopped, cleaned his wounds and took him to a safe place.
Jesus says to us: “Go and do likewise.” This week, look for someone who needs help, at school, at home or on the road, and help them!

homily: Dear friends, today is May Day, the day many countries honour workers. The Church gives us a worker too: St Joseph, the carpenter of Nazareth, patron of the working class.

The first reading tells us that after the first sin God said to Adam: “By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread” (Genesis 3:19). But work itself is not a curse. Even before sin, God placed the man in the garden to till it and keep it (Genesis 2:15). Sin brought the thorns, the tiredness and the frustration.

Then the Son of God came and worked with human hands. For many years Jesus worked in Joseph's workshop. In the Gospel the people of Nazareth say, “Is not this the carpenter’s son?” (Matthew 13:55). They meant it as an insult. For us it is a joy: our Saviour knows what it is to be tired after a day's work.

Joseph never speaks in the Gospels. He listens to God and obeys. Solomon prays in the second reading for wisdom to labour at his side (Wisdom 9:10). Joseph had that wisdom: quiet, faithful, hard-working. And St Paul tells us, “whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus” (Colossians 3:17).

Today let us pray for all workers: for those without work, for those paid unjustly, for workers from other states living among us, and for our own children working far from home. And let us offer our own work to the Lord, so that it becomes a prayer. St Joseph, pray for us. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus had a father on earth who was a carpenter: St Joseph. Jesus helped him to make tables and doors.
When you do your homework or help at home, do it for Jesus. Then your work becomes a prayer, just like the work in Joseph's workshop!

homily: Dear friends, today we honour two apostles, Philip and James. Philip was a practical man from Bethsaida. When Jesus called him, he ran to his friend Nathanael and said, “Come and see” (John 1:46). James led the Church in Jerusalem, and the risen Lord appeared to him (1 Corinthians 15:7).

At the Last Supper Philip asked, “Lord, show us the Father, and we will be satisfied.” Jesus answered, “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father” (John 14:8–9). We do not need to search far for God. He has shown his face in Jesus.

Jesus also said, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life” (John 14:6). On Thursday he will go up to the Father. He does not leave us a map; he leaves us himself. To follow him is to be on the way to the Father's house.

Paul says, “woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!” (1 Corinthians 9:16). The apostles could not keep silent. They gave their lives for Christ. Like the righteous in the Book of Wisdom, they now stand with great confidence before God.
Each of us can be a little apostle. We can say to a friend, ‘Come and see.’ Let us ask Sts Philip and James for their courage and their faith. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Philip found Jesus and ran to his friend: ‘Come and see!’
Who is a friend you can bring to Jesus? Invite them to church, or tell them a story about Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, in two days we celebrate the Ascension. Today Jesus speaks about his return: “about that day or hour no one knows... Beware, keep alert” (Mark 13:32–33).

He tells of a master who goes on a journey and leaves each servant his work, and tells the doorkeeper to watch. That is the Church after the Ascension. The Lord has gone to the Father; the house is in our care. Each of us has a task.

He may come “in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or at dawn” (Mark 13:35). Those were the hours of the night of the Passion, when the disciples slept. After the Resurrection they learned to watch. The Church still keeps watch in her evening and night prayer.

Peter says the day of the Lord will come like a thief, and asks, “what sort of persons ought you to be”? We wait for “new heavens and a new earth, where righteousness is at home” (2 Peter 3:11, 13). Let us live holy lives and care for God's creation while we wait.
At every Qurbana we proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. Let us say with the first Christians, Maranatha, come, Lord Jesus, and keep awake. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told us to stay awake for him, like a doorkeeper waiting for the master to come home.
How do we stay awake for Jesus? By praying, being kind and doing our work well every day.

homily: Dear friends, tomorrow is the Ascension. Today Jesus speaks to us like a friend who is going away: “I have said these things to you so that my joy may be in you, and that your joy may be complete” (John 15:11).
He gives us one commandment: “love one another as I have loved you” (John 15:12). How did he love us? “No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.”
Then he says something wonderful: “I have called you friends” (John 15:15). Not servants, but friends. And he chose us to go and bear fruit that will last.
Paul tells us to be “imitators of God, as beloved children” (Ephesians 5:1). That means living in love, keeping our hearts and words pure, and instead of vulgar talk, giving thanks.
Tonight, let us speak to Jesus as a friend, and tomorrow come to the Holy Qurbana to celebrate his Ascension with joy. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus calls you his friend! A friend shares, helps and loves.
Tomorrow Jesus goes up to heaven, but he is still our friend. Talk to him tonight before you sleep.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated the Ascension of our Lord. The disciples watched him go up, and then they went back to Jerusalem, to the upper room, to pray. Today we begin to pray with them.

The Gospel says: “The one who comes from above is above all.” Jesus came from the Father, and now he has returned to the Father. He is not one good teacher among many. He is above all. And “the Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.” The hands that were nailed to the Cross now hold the whole world, and they hold each of us.

Then comes a beautiful line: “he gives the Spirit without measure.” Jesus had said, if I go, I will send the Advocate to you. So the Ascension is not a goodbye; it is the beginning of a gift. For nine days the apostles prayed with Mary, the mother of Jesus, waiting for that gift. This was the first novena of the Church. Let us pray it with them until Pentecost.

Today is also the First Friday. We look at the Heart of Jesus, pierced on the Cross, from which came blood and water. From that open Heart the Spirit is poured out on the Church. Let us come to confession, receive him in the Holy Qurbana, and ask his Heart for the gift of the Spirit.

And Paul tells us how to live these days: “forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal.” God's call is an upward call: where Christ has gone, we are called to follow. Let us not sit down on the track and cry over yesterday's fall. Let us get up and run toward him. Come, Holy Spirit! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, yesterday Jesus went up to heaven. But he did not leave us alone! He promised to send the Holy Spirit.
For nine days the disciples prayed with Mary, waiting for the Holy Spirit. Can you pray with them? Every day until Pentecost, say: ‘Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart!’

homily: Dear friends, today the Gospel takes us to the river Jordan, where John the Baptist is preaching. Many religious leaders come to him, and he tells them: “Bear fruit worthy of repentance.”

He warns them not to say, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ We can say similar things: I was baptised as a baby, my family is old Catholic, my parish is ancient. Thank God for all that! But God looks for fruit. What fruit is in my life today?

Then John says: one more powerful than I is coming; “He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.” This promise came true at Pentecost, when tongues of fire rested on the disciples. In these nine days we pray for that fire. It does not destroy us; it burns away the chaff and keeps the wheat, as the wind does on the threshing floor.

Paul speaks of an undivided heart. Some are called to give themselves wholly to the Lord in priesthood or religious life. Others are called to marriage, which is also holy. Every one of us is called to “unhindered devotion to the Lord” in our own state of life.

On this Saturday of May let us look to Mary. Her heart was never divided; she belonged wholly to God, and she was a loving mother. She prayed with the apostles for the Spirit. Let us ask her today: Mother, pray with us, that the fire of the Spirit may come on us at Pentecost. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said that Jesus would give us the Holy Spirit and fire. Fire gives light and warmth.
When the Holy Spirit comes into your heart, he makes it warm with love and bright with goodness. Ask him today: ‘Holy Spirit, make my heart warm and bright!’

homily: Dear friends, today the Gospel takes us to a well in Samaria at noon. Jesus is tired, and he sits down. A woman comes to draw water, and Jesus asks her: “Give me a drink.”

She is surprised. Jews and Samaritans did not mix, and a Jewish teacher did not talk alone with a Samaritan woman. But Jesus crosses those walls. He is not ashamed to ask. God often begins with us like this: not with an order, but with a request. He asks for a little of our time, so that he can give us much more.

Jesus says: “If you knew the gift of God,” you would have asked me, and I would have given you living water. Whoever drinks ordinary water will be thirsty again. But “the water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.” This living water is the Holy Spirit. Jesus has now gone up to the Father, and the Spirit is about to be poured out. In this novena, let us bring him our thirst.

Paul tells the Thessalonians: God chose you as first fruits. Stand firm and hold fast to the traditions you were taught. Our Church received the faith from St Thomas, and our grandparents handed it to us. These traditions are channels through which the living water has reached us. Let us keep them and hand them on.
The woman said, “Sir, give me this water.” Let that be our prayer today: Lord, give us this water. Fill us with your Spirit at Pentecost. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus was thirsty, and he asked a woman for water. Then he told her about a special water that he gives, the Holy Spirit.
When we pray, the Holy Spirit fills our heart like a little spring of water that never dries. Say today: ‘Jesus, give me your living water!’

homily: Dear friends, a man in the crowd asks Jesus, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the family inheritance with me.” How often we hear such quarrels in our own families: over land, over the house, over money.

Jesus does not take sides. He goes to the root: “Take care! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; for one's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.” A property can be divided fairly, and still the heart can be full of greed. Jesus wants to heal the heart.

Then he tells the story of a rich man. His land gave a great harvest, and he said: I will build bigger barns, and then I will rest, eat, drink and be merry. He spoke only to himself. No God, no neighbour, no poor man in his plans. And God said: “You fool! This very night your life is being demanded of you.” All his grain was left behind.

Paul tells the Corinthians: be careful that your liberty does not become a stumbling block to the weak. The weak brother is someone “for whom Christ died”. “Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.” Our rights and our riches are given to us for others.

In these days before Pentecost we ask for the greatest treasure, the Holy Spirit. He fills not full barns but open hands. Let us empty one barn this week, make peace in our families, and be rich toward God. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a man who kept all his grain for himself in big barns and never shared. God called him foolish!
Jesus wants us to be ‘rich toward God’. How? By sharing! This week, share one of your toys, snacks or pencils with someone, and you will be rich toward God.

homily: Dear friends, on the night before he died, Jesus lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed: “Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you.” The hour was the Cross, and Jesus called it glory, because on the Cross God's love was shown to the world.

We read this prayer after the Ascension because it has been answered: Jesus has returned to the glory of the Father. But he has not stopped praying. He “always lives to make intercession” for us. In this novena, we join our prayer to his.

Jesus says: “This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” Eternal life begins now. To know God is not only to know facts about him; it is to love him and live with him, as a friend. A child who talks to Jesus has begun eternal life.

John tells us: “God is love, and those who abide in love abide in God.” God has given us his Spirit so that we can love. And “perfect love casts out fear.” We do not need to live afraid of God. But John adds: if you say you love God and hate your brother, you are a liar. Love for God must reach the brother we can see.
Let us ask the Holy Spirit today for this love: love that takes away fear, and love that reaches the people around us. Come, Holy Spirit! Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, John says: God is love! God loves you more than anyone can.
When we love one another, God lives in us. And when we know how much God loves us, we are not afraid. Today, say: ‘Jesus, I love you, and I am not afraid!’

homily: Dear friends, the First Letter of John begins with an old apostle's memory: “what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands, concerning the word of life.” John had touched Jesus. Our faith rests on a real meeting with a real person.

Now the Lord has ascended. How do we meet him? Through the witness of the apostles, handed on in the Church. “We declare to you what we have seen and heard so that you also may have fellowship with us.” We received this witness from St Thomas, who touched the Lord's wounds.

In the Gospel, large crowds follow Jesus. He turns and says: unless you put me before father and mother, before even your own life, you cannot be my disciple. He does not ask us to love our families less, but to love him most. “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.” A crowd follows for a day; a disciple follows to the end.

Jesus speaks of a man who builds a tower without counting the cost, and cannot finish. Many of us have begun towers: a promise at a retreat, a resolution after confession. Let us finish them. And he speaks of salt that loses its taste. Faith that becomes only a habit loses its taste. Let us restore it.

Today the Latin Church remembers Our Lady of Fatima. Mary asked three children to pray and offer sacrifices. She herself counted the cost at Nazareth and paid it at the Cross. In the upper room she prayed for the Spirit. Let us ask her to pray for us, that the Spirit may give us courage to follow to the end. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: before you build a big tower, think if you can finish it! Following Jesus is like building a tower: we must keep going even when it is hard.
At Fatima, Mary asked three children to pray every day. You can pray too! Today, say a Hail Mary for someone who is far from Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, today we keep the feast of St Matthias, Mar Mathias Shleeha. We know only one story about him, and it happened in these very days, between the Ascension and Pentecost, when the apostles were praying in the upper room with Mary the mother of Jesus (Acts 1:14).

Judas had betrayed the Lord, and one of the twelve places was empty. Peter stood up and said that someone who had walked with Jesus from the beginning must become “a witness with us to his resurrection” (Acts 1:22). That is what an apostle is: a witness of the Risen Lord.

They proposed two men, Joseph Justus and Matthias, and they prayed: “Lord, you know everyone’s heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen” (Acts 1:24). Not whom we like, but whom you have chosen. The lot fell on Matthias. And Joseph Justus went home without complaint. Both are lessons for us.

Samuel thought the tall Eliab must be God's choice, but God said: “the LORD looks on the heart” (1 Samuel 16:7). The youngest boy, out with the sheep, was anointed. Paul says the same: God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong, so that no one may boast before God (1 Corinthians 1:27–29).

Jesus thanks the Father for revealing these things to infants, and he invites: “Come to me, all you that are weary… and I will give you rest” (Matthew 11:28). The apostles were simple men who learned from his gentle and humble heart. Our Church, the Church of Mar Thoma, received the faith from such apostles.

Let us pray before our decisions, as the first Church did. Let us not judge by appearance. And as we wait with Mary for the Holy Spirit, let us be witnesses of the Resurrection, each in our own place. Alleluia! Amen.
kids: Children, there were twelve apostles, but one left Jesus. So the others prayed with Mother Mary and asked God to choose a new apostle. God chose Matthias!
God does not look at how tall or strong or clever we are. He looks at our heart. Let us keep our heart full of love for Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, on this last day of the Season of the Resurrection, the eve of Pentecost, our Church honours the Blessed Virgin Mary as Protectress of Harvest. In the lands where our East Syriac tradition was born, mid-May is the time of the grain harvest, and it is fitting to place our fields under the care of the Mother of Christ, the Bread of life.

The first reading tells Israel to keep “the festival of harvest, of the first fruits of your labor” (Exodus 23:16). That harvest festival was counted fifty days from Passover. Its Greek name is Pentecost. Tomorrow we keep that very festival, the day on which the Holy Spirit came and the first harvest of the Church was gathered: three thousand people baptised.

Joel promises a ruined land: “The threshing floors shall be full of grain” (Joel 2:24). Then he promises more: “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh” (Joel 2:28). Our farmers know what it is to wait for the rain. On this eve of Pentecost, Mary teaches us to wait for the greater rain, the Holy Spirit, as she waited with the apostles.
Paul reminds us that “the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable” (Romans 11:29). God is faithful to Israel, his first harvest, the people of Mary. And God wishes to show mercy to all.

Jesus says: “it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost” (Matthew 18:14). Our Mother does not forget one sheaf in the field. She prays for every child, especially the one who has gone astray.

So let us bring Mary our fields and our work, our children near and far, and our hearts. Let us forgive whoever has hurt us, so that our heart may be good soil tomorrow for the Holy Spirit. Holy Mother of God, pray for us. Alleluia! Amen.
