kids: Children, who gives us rice and bread? God gives the rain and the sun, and farmers work hard. Today we ask Mother Mary to take care of the farmers and the fields.
Tomorrow is Pentecost, the birthday of the Church, when God sent the Holy Spirit. Let us ask Mary to help us get our hearts ready!

homily: Dear friends, yesterday was Pentecost, the birthday of the Church. Today, the first weekday of the Season of the Apostles, the Church honours Mary as Mother of the Church. She was in the upper room with the apostles when the Spirit came (Acts 1:14).

At the Cross Jesus said to the beloved disciple, “Here is your mother” (John 19:27). In that disciple, we were all given a Mother. St Paul VI proclaimed her Mother of the Church in 1964, and Pope Francis set this memorial on the Monday after Pentecost.

Paul tells the Corinthians that when they come together each one has a gift, and “Let all things be done for building up” (1 Corinthians 14:26). Speak in turn, listen to one another, “for God is a God not of disorder but of peace” (14:33). Mary is the model: she pondered in silence, and her few words built up: “Do whatever he tells you.”

Jesus thanks the Father for revealing his secrets to infants, and says: “learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart” (Matthew 11:29). Mary was the little one, the humble servant. She learned and lived the gentleness of God, and she leads us to her Son, who gives rest to the weary.

Let us take Mary into our homes as the beloved disciple did. Let our parish meetings and prayer groups be places of peace, where each gift builds up. And let us bring our burdens to Jesus, with our Mother beside us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus gave his own mother to us! Mary is the Mother of the whole Church. When you are sad or afraid, you can say: “Mother Mary, pray for me,” and she will take you to Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus is leaving Jericho on his way to Jerusalem and the Cross. Two blind men by the road hear that he is passing and cry out: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!” (Matthew 20:30).

The crowd tells them to be quiet. But they shout even louder. There is always a crowd that tries to silence our prayer: shame, tiredness, people who say prayer is useless. Let us learn from the blind men to cry louder. Our liturgy repeats again and again, Lord, have mercy.

“Jesus stood still.” The Lord on his way to the Cross stops for two beggars. He asks, “What do you want me to do for you?” They say, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.” Moved with compassion, he touches their eyes, and they see, and they follow him (Matthew 20:32–34).

Paul praises the Thessalonians: their faith is growing and their love increasing, even under persecution. He prays that God will make them “worthy of his call” (2 Thessalonians 1:11). That is the portrait of the Church of the apostles: eyes opened, faith growing, love increasing, steadfast in trial.

In this Season of the Apostles let us cry to the Lord for mercy, tell him honestly what we need, and when he opens our eyes, follow him. Let us also pray for our brothers and sisters who suffer for their faith. Amen.
kids: Children, two blind men shouted to Jesus, “Lord, have mercy on us!” People said, “Be quiet!” but they shouted louder. Jesus stopped, touched their eyes, and they could see! Jesus always stops when we call him.

homily: Dear friends, three days after Pentecost Jesus tells us how his Church grows. “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed” (Matthew 13:31), the smallest of seeds, that becomes a tree where the birds of the air make their nests.

The Church began with about one hundred and twenty people in an upper room. Today she is in every land, and the birds of every nation find shelter in her branches. Our own Church in Kerala began, as tradition holds, with Mar Thoma and a few families. God's work starts small and grows slowly, and it is God who gives the growth.

Then Jesus says the kingdom is like yeast mixed into three measures of flour until all is leavened (13:33). Yeast is hidden, but it changes everything. Christians are meant to be such yeast in offices, fields, schools and homes: not apart from the world, but mixed into it, without losing their strength.

Paul warns the Corinthians about their Lord's Supper: “if we judged ourselves, we would not be judged” (1 Corinthians 11:31). Before we receive the Body of the Lord we examine our conscience. And he adds: “when you come together to eat, wait for one another” (11:33). The Eucharist makes us one body with the poor and the last.
So let us not despise small beginnings, let us be yeast in the world, and let us come to the Holy Qurbana prepared and attentive to one another. Amen.
kids: Children, a mustard seed is tiny, like a speck of dust, but it grows into a big plant where birds can sit! Jesus says small good things done with love grow big with God. What small good thing will you do today?

homily: Dear friends, four days after Pentecost the readings speak of a promise and a Temple.

Hebrews quotes Jeremiah: God will make a new covenant. “I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts.” At Sinai the law was written on stone. At Pentecost the Holy Spirit wrote it on human hearts. That is the new covenant: not a law outside us, but love within us.

Hebrews ends the promise with these words: “I will remember their sins no more.” The new covenant begins with mercy. God first gave this promise to Israel; he has not taken back his love for them, and he has welcomed us too.

In the Gospel Jesus finds the Temple full of buying and selling. He drives the merchants out: “Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!” He does this out of love for his Father's house. Then he says, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking of his own body, which rose on the third day.
Now we too are God's temple, and the Spirit lives in us. Let Jesus clean that temple: let him drive out greed, anger and every bargain we try to make with God.
Today our Church also remembers the first gathering of our Synod of Bishops in 1993. Let us pray for our bishops, and let us keep our churches and our hearts as houses of prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus got very upset when people turned God's house into a noisy market. He loved his Father's house!
Did you know that you are God's house too? The Holy Spirit lives in your heart. Keep it clean with kind words, prayers and saying sorry when you do wrong.

homily: Dear friends, today our Church keeps the Friday of Gold, the first Friday after Pentecost. It remembers the first miracle the apostles worked after the Holy Spirit came.

Peter and John go to the Temple at three in the afternoon to pray. At the Beautiful Gate a man lame from birth asks them for money. Peter looks at him and says, “Look at us.” Then: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.” He takes his hand, and the man walks, leaps and praises God.
Isaiah had promised this: “then the lame shall leap like a deer.” The age of the Messiah has come, and the Church continues his work in his Name.

Peter tells the crowd that it was not his power but the God of Abraham who healed the man. He calls them “friends” and says, “I know that you acted in ignorance.” He invites them to repent and receive blessing. The Church blames no people for the Cross; we all need that call to repentance.

Paul tells us the secret behind the miracle: love. Without love, all gifts are nothing. “Love is patient; love is kind… Love never ends.” Peter had no gold, but he had love. And Jesus, at the gate of Nain, had compassion on a widow and gave her son back to her.
So today, do not say, I have nothing to give. You have the name of Jesus, a hand to hold out and a heart to love. That is the gold of the Church. Amen.
kids: Children, Peter and John had no money at all! But they met a man who could not walk, and Peter said, ‘What I have I give you: in the name of Jesus, walk!’ And the man jumped and danced!
You can give something better than money too: a smile, a helping hand, a prayer. That is your gold!

opts.a: At three o'clock, at the Beautiful Gate
intro: Peter and John went up to the Temple at the hour of prayer. At the gate called Beautiful sat a man who had never once walked in. On the Friday of Gold he walks, leaps and praises God inside.

sub: Evening, morning and noon I will pray.
The Spirit does not cancel prayer.
points.apply: Keep a fixed hour of prayer each day this week.

sub: Lame from birth, carried every day.
Placed at the gate, never inside.
Those left at our church doors.
points.apply: Notice and greet someone who stays at the edges of the parish.

sub: He enters the Temple with them.
The joy of being brought in.
points.apply: Praise God aloud for one gift you have received.

concl: The apostles prayed, saw the one at the gate and brought him in.
The gold of the Church is to bring people from the gate into God's house with joy.
opts.resolve: This week I will keep a fixed hour of prayer and reach out to one person on the edges of our parish.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the Friday of Gold, when our Church remembers the first miracle of the apostles after Pentecost. Luke begins simply: one day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, at three o'clock in the afternoon (Acts 3:1). The Holy Spirit had come upon them, yet they kept their hours of prayer.

The Psalm says: evening and morning and at noon I utter my complaint and moan, and he will hear my voice (Psalm 55:17). The Spirit does not make prayer unnecessary. He makes it alive. If we want the power of Pentecost, let us also keep a fixed hour of prayer each day.

At the gate called Beautiful sat a man lame from birth. People carried him there every day to beg (Acts 3:2). He lived at the gate of beauty but had never entered. In the old law, those who were lame could not serve at the altar (Leviticus 21:18). He had been left outside all his life. How many people sit at the edges of our parishes: the poor, the disabled, the lonely, those who feel unworthy?

Peter took him by the right hand and raised him up, and immediately his feet and ankles were made strong. Jumping up, he stood and began to walk, and he entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God (Acts 3:7–8). David once danced before the ark with all his might. This man, who had never walked, now danced into God's house.

That is the gold of the Church: not money, but the name of Jesus that brings people from the gate into the house of God. Let us keep our hour of prayer, notice those who sit at our doors, and bring them in with us to the Holy Qurbana, praising God. Amen.

opts.a: Are you the one who is to come?
intro: Even John the Baptist, in prison, sent to ask Jesus: are you the one? Jesus did not scold him. He pointed to what God was doing. Today's Gospel speaks to all who struggle with doubt.

sub: John hears in prison of Jesus' deeds.
points.apply: Bring your honest questions to God in prayer.

points.h: Tell what you have seen and heard
sub: The blind see, the lame walk.
points.apply: Write down three things God has done in your life.

points.h: Blessed is anyone who takes no offense
sub: Love sees in a mirror, dimly, and trusts.
points.apply: When God does not act as you expected, make an act of trust.

concl: Doubt brought to Jesus becomes deeper faith.
His works answer our questions, and love trusts where it cannot yet see.
opts.resolve: This week I will bring my questions to God and remember three things he has done for me.
homily: Dear friends, in today's Gospel even John the Baptist has a question. He is in Herod's prison. He hears of what Jesus is doing, and he sends two of his disciples to ask: are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another? (Luke 7:19). The greatest of the prophets wonders.

There is no shame in an honest question brought to God. The Psalms are full of them: how long, O LORD? Will you forget me forever? (Psalm 13:1). God is not offended when we bring our questions to him. He is grieved only when we walk away with them.

Jesus does not argue. He says: go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them (Luke 7:22). These are the signs Isaiah promised for the anointed one who would bring good news to the oppressed (Isaiah 61:1). The answer to doubt is to look again at what God is doing.

And he adds: blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me (Luke 7:23). John expected a Messiah of fire and judgment. Jesus came with mercy. Isaiah had said that the Lord would become a stone one strikes against. Paul, in today's Epistle, says that now we see in a mirror, dimly, but love bears all things and hopes all things (1 Corinthians 13:7, 12). Love trusts where it cannot yet see.

On this Friday of Gold, when the apostles began to work the same signs in Jesus' name, let us bring our questions to him. Let us write down three things he has done for us. And when he does not act as we expected, let us trust him still, and receive him at the Holy Qurbana. Amen.
Dear friends, on this Saturday after Pentecost, Paul describes the Church as a body. “For just as the body is one and has many members… so it is with Christ.”
The Church is the Body of Christ, and he is the Head. In Baptism we were placed in that Body, and we drank the one Spirit.

Paul jokes about a foot that says, I am not a hand, so I do not belong. And an ear that says, I am not an eye. How foolish! Every part is needed. “God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.”
In our parish there is no unimportant member: the one who sings, the one who teaches, the one who cleans, the one who prays in a sickbed at home. Each is placed by God.
In the Gospel the people follow Jesus because he gave them bread. Jesus says: work for the food that endures for eternal life. And the work of God is this: to believe in the One whom he has sent.
Like the Blessed Virgin Mary, who prayed with the apostles, let us seek Jesus for himself, and serve him gladly in the place he has given us. Amen.
kids: Children, can your eye say to your hand, ‘I don't need you’? No! Your body needs every part. The Church is like that: everyone is important, even the smallest child.
What is your part? Maybe singing, maybe helping, maybe praying for others. Do it with joy, because you belong to Jesus' Body!

homily: Dear friends, today Paul writes from prison to the Christians of Philippi: “join in imitating me.” He is not boasting. He is a runner still pressing on, and he asks them to run with him.

Then he weeps for those who live as enemies of the Cross, whose god is the belly and whose minds are set on earthly things. And he reminds us: “our citizenship is in heaven.” We belong to God's kingdom, and we wait for the Saviour who will transform our weak bodies to be like his glorious body.

In the Gospel Lazarus has died. Martha runs to meet Jesus and says honestly, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” Jesus does not scold her. He says, “Your brother will rise again.”
Martha thinks of the last day, but Jesus says, “I am the resurrection and the life.” The resurrection is not only a future day; it is a Person, and he is here.
Jesus asks her, “Do you believe this?” Martha answers, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God.”
Today he asks the same question of each of us, especially those who are grieving. Let us answer with Martha, and live as citizens of heaven. Amen.
kids: Children, Martha was sad because her brother Lazarus had died. But Jesus told her, ‘I am the resurrection and the life.’ That means Jesus is stronger than death!
When someone we love goes to heaven, we can be sad, but we can also say like Martha: ‘Yes, Lord, I believe!’

homily: Dear friends, in today's reading Paul asks, “Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord?” He has met the Risen Lord, and the Church at Corinth is the proof of his mission.
Paul shows that those who preach the Gospel have a right to be supported, as a soldier, a farmer or a shepherd lives by his work. The Church still asks us to support her ministers and her mission.

But then Paul says that he gave up this right: “we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.” He worked with his own hands so that no one could say he preached for money.

In the Gospel Jesus has spoken about eating his Body and drinking his Blood. Many disciples find this too hard and leave. Jesus does not change his words. He asks the Twelve, “Do you also wish to go away?”
Peter answers, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.” Peter does not understand everything, but he knows that life is found only in Jesus.
On Thursday we celebrate the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ. Let us renew our faith that Jesus is truly present in the Holy Qurbana, and let us say with Peter: Lord, to whom can we go? Amen.
kids: Children, once Jesus said something very hard to understand, and many people walked away. Jesus asked his friends, ‘Will you go away too?’ Peter said, ‘Lord, where would we go? Only you give us eternal life!’
When something is hard, stay close to Jesus like Peter. On Thursday we celebrate Jesus in the Holy Qurbana. Say thank you to him!

homily: Dear friends, today Jesus makes a promise that we can hold on to all our lives: “anyone who comes to me I will never drive away” (John 6:37). No sin is too big and no person is too small. The door of Jesus is never shut to one who comes.

Why? Because Jesus came down from heaven to do the will of the Father, and the Father's will is that not one of those given to him should be lost. Jesus says it again and again: I will raise them up on the last day.

But some who heard him grumbled: is not this the son of Joseph? We know his family. They knew him too well to listen to him. We too have known Jesus since childhood. Let us ask for new ears, so that familiarity does not hide him from us.

Saint Paul speaks to Christians who thought the body did not matter. He says: your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit; you are not your own; you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body (1 Corinthians 6:19–20). The Spirit who came at Pentecost lives in us.

So let us take care of this temple. Let us keep it clean from what enslaves, use it to serve, care for the bodies of the sick and the old with reverence, and receive into it the Body of Christ, who will raise it up on the last day. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says he will never send away anyone who comes to him. You can always run to Jesus, even when you have done something wrong. And your body is like a little church where the Holy Spirit lives. So take care of it, and never hurt anyone else's body!

homily: Dear friends, today the Church does what she did on Maundy Thursday, but now in the full light of Easter and Pentecost: she gives thanks for the Body and Blood of Christ. The word Qurbana means offering. In every Qurbana Christ offers himself, and gives himself to us.

Long before Christ, a king and priest named Melchizedek came out to meet Abram with bread and wine and blessed him. The Bible calls Jesus a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek. At our altar too, bread and wine are offered, and they become the Body and Blood of the eternal Priest.

Through Malachi God complains about careless worship: blind and lame animals, the leftovers. But he promises: from the rising of the sun to its setting, a pure offering will be made to my name in every place (Malachi 1:11). The first Christians saw here the Eucharist, offered every hour somewhere in the world. Let us never give God our leftovers.

Paul hands on what he received: on the night he was betrayed, Jesus took bread and said, “This is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” Then Paul warns: examine yourselves, and only then eat (1 Corinthians 11:24, 28). Let us come to Communion with a clean heart, reconciled with God and with our neighbour.

In the Gospel Jesus says: my flesh is true food and my blood is true drink (John 6:55). Not only a sign, but truly himself. It looks like bread, but it is the Lord. That is why we kneel, we fast before Communion, we keep silence, and we adore him.

And Jesus says: whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in them (John 6:56). We carry him out of the church. In these days many of our parishes walk in procession with the Blessed Sacrament. Let our whole life be such a procession, carrying Christ to our homes and streets. Amen.
kids: Children, at the Holy Qurbana the priest says the words of Jesus: “This is my body.” Then the bread becomes Jesus himself! It still looks like bread, but it is Jesus.
That is why we are quiet and we kneel. When you see the priest lift up the Host, say softly in your heart: “My Lord and my God!”

opts.a: Lord, to whom can we go?
intro: When Jesus said, my flesh is true food, many disciples left him. He did not call them back with a softer teaching. He asked the Twelve: do you also wish to go away?

sub: Whoever eats this bread will live forever.
points.apply: Prepare for each Communion with a short prayer of thanksgiving.

sub: Jesus did not change his words.
Choose this day whom you will serve.
points.apply: Learn what the Church teaches about the Real Presence and share it with your family.

points.h: You have the words of eternal life
points.apply: Spend some time in adoration this week, saying Peter's words.

concl: Jesus did not water down the mystery of his Body and Blood.
With Peter we answer: Lord, to whom can we go?
opts.resolve: This week I will spend time before the Blessed Sacrament and say: Lord, to whom can we go?
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in today's Gospel Jesus says: this is the bread that came down from heaven, not like that which your ancestors ate, and they died. But the one who eats this bread will live forever (John 6:58). In the desert God fed Israel with manna each morning. It sustained their bodies for a time. The bread Christ gives is himself, and it gives eternal life.

But the Gospel goes on. When many of his disciples heard it, they said: this teaching is difficult; who can accept it? (John 6:60). And many turned back and no longer went about with him. Notice: Jesus did not call them back and say, I only meant a symbol. He let them go, because he had spoken the truth. The bread is truly his flesh; the cup is truly his blood.

Then he turned to the Twelve and asked: do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). It is like Joshua's challenge to Israel: choose this day whom you will serve (Joshua 24:15). Today many people, even baptised Christians, find the mystery of the Eucharist too hard. The question comes to each of us: will I stay?

Simon Peter answered: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God (John 6:68–69). Peter did not understand everything. But he knew Jesus, and he trusted him. The Psalm invites us: O taste and see that the LORD is good (Psalm 34:8).

On this Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ, let us learn what the Church teaches and share it with our children. Let us spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this week. And when we receive him at the Holy Qurbana, let us say with Peter: Lord, to whom can we go? Amen.

intro: The Eucharist is not only Christ given to each of us. It makes us one body. Paul warns that a Communion which forgets the poor brother does not discern the body.

points.h: We who are many are one body
sub: Unity as the fruit of Communion.
points.apply: Pray after Communion for the person sitting next to you.

sub: Divisions at the Lord's supper in Corinth.
Some go hungry, others are full.
The poor belong at the table.
points.apply: Share a meal this week with someone poor or lonely.

points.h: Carrying the Lord through our streets
points.apply: Join the Eucharistic procession or adoration in your parish.

concl: The Body of Christ received makes the Body of Christ, the Church.
We discern his body in the bread and in the poor.
opts.resolve: This week I will pray for my neighbour after Communion and share a meal with someone poor or lonely.
homily: Dear friends, Paul asks the Corinthians: the cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ? Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread (1 Corinthians 10:16–17).

The Eucharist does two things at once. It gives us Christ, truly present, Body and Blood, soul and divinity. And it makes us one body in him. Saint Augustine told his people: receive what you are, the Body of Christ. The Psalm says: how very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity (Psalm 133:1). After Communion, let us pray for the person beside us.

But in Corinth something was wrong. When they gathered for the Lord's supper, the rich ate first and the poor went hungry (1 Corinthians 11:21). Paul said: that is not really to eat the Lord's supper. And he warned that all who eat and drink without discerning the body eat and drink judgment against themselves (1 Corinthians 11:29). Amos had condemned those who lay on beds of ivory and were not grieved over the ruin of their people (Amos 6:4–6). To discern the body is to see Christ in the bread, and also in the poor brother at the door.

In these days many of our parishes carry the Blessed Sacrament in procession. David danced before the ark of the LORD as it was brought into the city (2 Samuel 6:14). At Emmaus the two disciples recognised the Lord in the breaking of the bread, and their hearts burned (Luke 24:30–32). The procession shows that Christ does not stay locked in the church. He walks with his people.

So let us come to the Holy Qurbana as one family. Let us pray for our neighbour after Communion. Let us share a meal this week with someone poor or lonely. And let us walk behind the Blessed Sacrament, carrying the Lord into our homes and streets. Amen.

Dear friends, yesterday we celebrated the Body and Blood of Christ. Today Jesus tells us how we come to that bread: “It is written in the prophets, ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to me” (John 6:45).

Before we eat, we listen. That is why every Qurbana begins with the Word: the readings, the Gospel and the homily. God teaches us first, and then feeds us. Let us not arrive late for the readings, as if only the second part mattered.

Then Jesus says: “I am the bread of life.” The ancestors ate manna in the desert and still died. But whoever eats the bread that comes down from heaven will not die. Jesus gives a life that death cannot destroy. And he says first: whoever believes has eternal life. We come to the altar with faith.

Paul tells the proud Corinthians: the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. They were fighting over their favourite preachers, Paul, Apollos and Cephas. Paul says: all of them are yours, and you belong to Christ (1 Corinthians 3:21–23).

So let us become humble learners, like children. Let us not divide our parishes over preachers and movements. All the gifts of the Church are given to us, so that we may belong more fully to Christ, who is the bread of life. Amen.
kids: Children, in the desert God gave his people a special bread called manna. But Jesus says he is an even better bread: the bread of life! At the Holy Qurbana we first listen to God's word, and then we receive Jesus. So listen carefully to the readings next Sunday!

homily: Dear friends, a huge crowd followed Jesus, and there was nothing to eat. Philip counted the cost: six months' wages would not be enough. Andrew found a boy with five barley loaves and two fish, and said, “But what are they among so many people?” (John 6:9).

The boy gave what he had. It was not enough. But Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks and distributed them, and five thousand ate as much as they wanted. Those are the words of the Holy Qurbana: he took, gave thanks, and gave. Never think your gift is too small for God.

Then Jesus said, “Gather up the fragments left over, so that nothing may be lost” (John 6:12). Twelve baskets were filled. The Lord gives in abundance, but nothing is wasted, and no one is to be lost. Let us waste no food, and gather up the ones the world forgets.

Saint Paul says: the bread that we break is a sharing in the body of Christ; because there is one bread, we who are many are one body (1 Corinthians 10:16–17). Communion makes us one. So we cannot give our hearts to idols, to money, success or charms, and we cannot forget the hungry.
This is the last Saturday of the month of Mary. She gave the Lord her whole self, and he took flesh from her. Let us give him our five loaves today, and let him make them bread for many. Amen.
kids: Children, a boy gave Jesus his lunch: five small loaves and two fish. Jesus thanked God and fed five thousand people! And there were twelve baskets left over. Give Jesus what you have, even if it is small, and see what he can do with it!

homily: Dear friends, today is the last day of the month of Mary, and the Church celebrates the Visitation. The angel has left Nazareth, the Son of God has taken flesh in Mary's womb, and Mary hears that Elizabeth, old and once barren, is expecting a child. What does she do? “Mary set out and went with haste” (Luke 1:39).

The first thing Mary does after receiving Jesus is to carry him to someone who needs her. Her haste is the haste of love and joy. In this Season of the Apostles, the Church does the same: whoever has received Christ goes out to bring him to others.

When Mary greets Elizabeth, the child in Elizabeth's womb leaps for joy, and Elizabeth is filled with the Holy Spirit. She cries out, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” We say these words in every Hail Mary. And she calls Mary “the mother of my Lord” (Luke 1:43), the Mother of God.

Luke tells the story like the story of the ark of the covenant. David danced before the ark; John leaps before Jesus. The ark stayed three months in a house and brought blessing; Mary stays three months with Elizabeth. Mary is the new ark, the first tabernacle, carrying the living Bread to Elizabeth's home.

Elizabeth says, “blessed is she who believed” (Luke 1:45). Mary believed, and her faith became service. Saint Paul tells us how: let love be genuine, extend hospitality, rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep, associate with the lowly (Romans 12:9–16).

As we close the month of Mary, let us give her the gift she loves most: to believe God's word as she did, and to set out in haste to someone who needs us, carrying Jesus whom we have received in the Holy Qurbana. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary walked a long way over the hills to help her old cousin Elizabeth. When Mary said hello, baby John jumped for joy inside Elizabeth, because Jesus was there!
Like Mary, hurry to help someone this week: help Grandma, a little brother, or a friend. And every time you pray the Hail Mary, remember Elizabeth's happy words!

intro: Theme: “that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.”
On the last Sunday before the Ascension: the beautiful feet of the messenger, the door opened to the nations, the dividing wall broken down, and the prayer of Jesus for our unity.

sub: All the ends of the earth shall see salvation.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!
points.apply: Bring one word of hope this week to someone who is discouraged.

sub: Peter on the rooftop at Joppa.
A faithful man led step by step.
The door opened to the nations.
q: for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
The voice said to him again, a second time, “What God has made clean, you must not call profane.”
points.apply: Examine whom you look down on, and greet that person with respect this week.

sub: Once far off, now brought near.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the Lord; and I will heal them.
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.
points.apply: Take one step to heal an old quarrel in your family or neighbourhood.

points.h: That they may all be one
sub: Unity in the life of the Father and the Son.
So that the world may believe.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the unity of all Christians.

concl: Christ has broken down the walls that divide us and prayed that we may be one.
As we prepare for his Ascension on Thursday, let us carry his peace and live as one household, so that the world may believe.
2027-05-02.resolve: This week, pray daily for unity, heal one quarrel, and take part in the Holy Qurbana of the Ascension on Thursday.

intro: Theme: “While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.”
On the feast of the Ascension: Elijah's mantle and the promised Spirit, the call to witness, the one Mediator at the right hand of the Father, and the blessing that leaves great joy.

points.h: If you see me as I am being taken
sub: Elisha who would not leave his master.
A double share of the spirit.
It is to your advantage that I go away.
q: Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit.
Nevertheless I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
points.apply: Begin a novena to the Holy Spirit tomorrow, asking for one particular gift.

points.h: Why do you stand looking up toward heaven?
sub: He will come in the same way.
q: God has gone up with a shout, the Lord with the sound of a trumpet.
They said, “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven? This Jesus, who has been taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him go into heaven.”
points.apply: Choose one concrete act of witness this week: a word, a visit, an invitation.

sub: Our nature at the right hand of the Father.
He always lives to make intercession.
q: There is no umpire between us, who might lay his hand on us both.
For there is one God; there is also one mediator between God and humankind, Christ Jesus, himself human,
points.apply: Pray today for those in authority, naming them before God.

points.h: Lifting up his hands, he blessed them
sub: The last sight of the pierced hands.
q: Aaron lifted his hands toward the people and blessed them
While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
points.apply: Bless your children or family members tonight, and pray together for the coming of the Spirit.

concl: Christ our Head has entered heaven with our nature; he blesses us, intercedes for us and sends us his Spirit.
Let us not stand idly looking up, but return with joy to pray with Mary and to bear witness, until he comes again.
2027-05-06.resolve: Take part in the Qurbana of the Ascension, begin a novena to the Holy Spirit with your family, pray daily for all in authority, and give one act of witness this week.

intro: Theme: “Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, ‘Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?’ And I said, ‘Here am I; send me!’”
On the Sunday after the Ascension: the thrice-holy God who purifies and sends, the witness chosen in prayer with Mary, the self-emptying and exaltation of Christ, and the mission to all the world.

sub: Woe is me: the sinner before the Holy One.
The live coal from the altar.
q: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.
points.apply: Sing the angels' hymn at the Qurbana with attention, and receive Holy Communion as the live coal that purifies you.

sub: The question comes after the purification.
A hard mission and a holy seed.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.”
points.apply: Offer one concrete service to your parish or neighbourhood this week.

sub: The circle of the Twelve restored.
q: O LORD, you have searched me and known me.
Then they prayed and said, “Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which one of these two you have chosen.”
points.apply: Pray each day this week for the bishops of our Synod and for every decision your family must take.

points.h: Every tongue shall confess that Jesus Christ is Lord
q: By myself I have sworn, from my mouth has gone forth in righteousness a word that shall not return: “To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.”
So that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth, and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
points.apply: In one quarrel or competition this week, give the first place to the other.

concl: The Lord who emptied himself is exalted at the right hand of the Father, and from there he sends us and works with us.
Purified at the altar and praying with Mary, let us answer: Here am I; send me.
2027-05-09.resolve: This week, offer one service, pray daily for our bishops, choose the last place once, and pray the novena with Mary for the Holy Spirit.

intro: Theme: “All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.”
On the Feast of Pentecost: Sinai fulfilled, the Church born speaking, Babel undone, the gifts of the one Spirit, and the Spirit of truth who guides us into all the truth.

points.h: A priestly kingdom and a holy nation
q: but you shall be for me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation.
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God’s own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises this week, and offer each day to God as a member of his holy people.

points.h: Each heard in their own language
q: Therefore it was called Babel, because there the LORD confused the language of all the earth; and from there the LORD scattered them abroad over the face of all the earth.
And at this sound the crowd gathered and was bewildered, because each one heard them speaking in the native language of each.
points.apply: Pray for the unity of the Church in all her rites and languages, and speak of your faith to one person this week.

points.h: Varieties of gifts, the same Spirit
q: Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
points.apply: Offer one gift of yours this month to the service of your parish.

points.h: The Spirit of truth will guide you
sub: It is to your advantage that I go.
All that the Father has is mine.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth;
points.apply: Before each decision this week, pray: Come, Holy Spirit, guide me into the truth.

concl: The Spirit who came down on the apostles gathered with Mary makes us a holy people, one Church in many tongues, and gives each of us a gift for others.
As the Season of the Apostles begins, let us receive the fire and carry it out, as Mar Thoma carried it to our land.
2027-05-16.resolve: This week, pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each morning, pray the Angelus, and use one gift of yours for the common good.

intro: Theme: “God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.”

The feast of the Most Holy Trinity: the three visitors at Mamre, the God who is first and last, the love of the Father poured out through the Son and the Spirit, and the Spirit of truth who takes what is the Son's and gives it to us.

points.h: Three men at the oaks of Mamre
sub: Abraham at the door of his tent.
Three visitors addressed as one Lord.
God the guest, welcomed by hospitality.
q: He looked up and saw three men standing near him. When he saw them, he ran from the tent entrance to meet them, and bowed down to the ground.
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Invite one lonely or forgotten person to share a meal in your home this week.

points.h: I am the first, and I am the last
sub: The Creator who laid the foundations of the earth.
The One who calls and sends.
The God who teaches and leads.
q: Listen to me, O Jacob, and Israel, whom I called: I am He; I am the first, and I am the last.
I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
points.apply: Begin each day this week by asking the Father to lead you in the way you should go.

points.h: God's love poured into our hearts
sub: The Spirit, the love of God given to us.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
And hope does not disappoint us, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.
points.apply: Offer one present suffering to the Father, through Jesus, in the Spirit, and ask that it may produce hope.

points.h: All that the Father has is mine
sub: Things the disciples could not yet bear.
The Spirit of truth who guides into all truth.
The life of God shared with us.
q: The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
All that the Father has is mine. For this reason I said that he will take what is mine and declare it to you.
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross slowly each morning and evening, and pray the Glory Be with your family.

concl: The Trinity is not a distant puzzle but the life of God into which we were baptized: the Father loves us, the Son opens the way, the Spirit pours love into our hearts.
Let us welcome God in every guest, trust him in every suffering, and let the Spirit guide us into all the truth.
2027-05-23.resolve: This week, make the sign of the Cross with attention, welcome one guest as Abraham did, and pray the Glory Be at the beginning and end of each day.

intro: Theme: “He said, ‘The one who showed him mercy.’ Jesus said to him, ‘Go and do likewise.’”
On the Third Sunday of the Apostles: a people sent on from the mountain, a people who forgot their owner, the gifts of marriage and celibacy, and the Samaritan who became a neighbour.

points.h: You have stayed long enough at this mountain
sub: Horeb, the mountain of the covenant.
The apostles sent to the nations.
q: The Lord our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying, “You have stayed long enough at this mountain.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
points.apply: Take one step out of your comfortable circle this week in the service of the Gospel.

q: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s crib; but Israel does not know, my people do not understand.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son and wrapped him in bands of cloth, and laid him in a manger, because there was no place for them in the inn.
points.apply: Begin and end each day this week with prayer at the family altar.

points.h: Each has a particular gift from God
sub: Husband and wife belong to each other.
q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
I wish that all were as I myself am. But each has a particular gift from God, one having one kind and another a different kind.
points.apply: Married couples, pray together each night this week; everyone, pray for a priest or a sister by name.

sub: Moved with pity, he came near.
Christ the Samaritan, the Church the inn.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the Lord.
But a Samaritan while traveling came near him; and when he saw him, he was moved with pity.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of mercy this week for someone outside your own group.

concl: The Spirit of the apostles moves us off our mountains, reminds us whose we are, blesses every vocation and makes us neighbours.
Healed by Christ the Samaritan, we cannot pass by on the other side.
2027-05-30.resolve: This week, step out of your comfort, pray daily at the family altar, pray for marriages and vocations, and show mercy to someone outside your circle.

intro: Theme: “And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.”
On May Day, with St Joseph, Patron of the Working Class: work in God's plan, toil redeemed by the carpenter's Son, and wisdom that labours at our side.

points.h: By the sweat of your face
sub: Toil and thorns after the fall.
The Son of God enters our toil.
q: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the ground
Anyone unwilling to work should not eat.
points.apply: Do one task today that you have been avoiding, and offer its effort to Christ.

points.h: Is not this the carpenter's son?
sub: Joseph who taught a trade to the Son of God.
q: You shall eat the fruit of the labor of your hands; you shall be happy, and it shall go well with you.
Is not this the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary?
points.apply: Thank one ordinary worker today, a bus driver, a cleaner or a shopkeeper, and see Christ's dignity in them.

points.h: Do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus
sub: Wisdom that labours at my side.
q: that she may labor at my side, and that I may learn what is pleasing to you.
And whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
points.apply: Begin and end each working day this week with a short prayer to St Joseph.

concl: The Son of God worked at Joseph's bench, and so every honest work can become holy.
Let us offer our labour in his name, pay and seek just wages, and pray for all who toil.
2027-05-01.resolve: This week, offer your work each morning, thank one worker each day, and pray for those who labour far from home.

intro: Theme: “Jesus said to him, ‘I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.’”
On the feast of the apostles Philip and James: the Father seen in the Son, the way that is a Person, the duty to proclaim, and the confidence of the righteous.

sub: The longing of every human heart.
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
q: Moses said, “Show me your glory, I pray.”
Whoever has seen me has seen the Father.
points.apply: Spend some minutes today before a crucifix or icon, asking the Lord to show you the Father.

points.h: I am the way, and the truth, and the life
sub: Do not let your hearts be troubled.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Bring one troubled worry to Jesus in prayer today and leave it with him.

points.h: Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel
q: If I say, “I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,” then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones
woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
points.apply: Invite one person this week to come and see: to the Qurbana, to adoration or to a prayer meeting.

points.h: The righteous will stand with confidence
sub: The song of Moses at the sea.
The apostles who gave their lives.
q: Then the righteous will stand with great confidence in the presence of those who have oppressed them and those who make light of their labors.
Blessed is anyone who endures temptation. Such a one has stood the test and will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.
points.apply: Pray today for Christians who suffer for their faith, that they may stand firm.

concl: Philip and James saw the Father in the face of Jesus and gave their lives proclaiming him.
May we walk the way that is Christ and invite others to come and see.
2027-05-03.resolve: This week, pray the Creed slowly each day, invite one friend to meet Jesus, and pray for persecuted Christians.

intro: Theme: “Beware, keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.”
Two days before the Ascension: the hidden day, the servants left in charge, the night watches, and the new heavens and new earth.

sub: No one knows the day or hour.
The point is not curiosity but readiness.
Living each day as the Lord's.
q: For there is still a vision for the appointed time; it speaks of the end, and does not lie. If it seems to tarry, wait for it; it will surely come, it will not delay.
Beware, keep alert; for you do not know when the time will come.
points.apply: Each night this week, examine your day briefly before sleeping.

sub: The Master gone on a journey.
The house left in our hands.
q: So you, mortal, I have made a sentinel for the house of Israel
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.
points.apply: Do your daily duty this week as a service to the Lord who will return.

points.h: New heavens and a new earth
sub: The day of the Lord like a thief.
What sort of persons ought we to be?
q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.
But, in accordance with his promise, we wait for new heavens and a new earth, where righteousness is at home.
points.apply: Do one concrete thing this week to care for God's creation.

concl: The Lord who ascends will return; until then he has left us his house and our work.
Let us keep awake in prayer and holiness, waiting for the new creation.
2027-05-04.resolve: This week, examine your day each night, do your work as for the Lord, and care for creation in one practical way.

intro: Theme: “This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.”
On the eve of the Ascension: the joy of Jesus, the friendship he offers, and the call to imitate God in love, purity and thanksgiving.

sub: Live in love as Christ loved us.
q: You shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy.
Therefore be imitators of God, as beloved children, and live in love, as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us
points.apply: Choose one way this week to love as Christ loved: patiently, humbly, at a cost.

sub: Friends who know the Master's heart.
q: But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, the offspring of Abraham, my friend
but I have called you friends, because I have made known to you everything that I have heard from my Father.
points.apply: Spend some minutes each evening this week speaking to Jesus as to a friend.

sub: Thanksgiving in place of vulgar talk.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last
points.apply: Replace one habit of careless or unclean talk with a habit of thanksgiving.

concl: Before he ascends, Jesus calls us friends and sends us to love as he loved.
Let us imitate God as beloved children and bear fruit that will last.
2027-05-05.resolve: This week, do a hidden act of love each day, speak to Jesus as a friend each evening, and thank God for three gifts before sleeping.

intro: Theme: “He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.”
The day after the Ascension and the first day of the novena: the Lord above all, the Spirit poured out from his open Heart, and the upward call that sets our life in motion.

points.h: The One from above is above all
sub: He came from the Father and has returned to him.
Faith as a seal on the truth of God.
q: Lift up your heads, O gates! and be lifted up, O ancient doors! that the King of glory may come in.
The one who comes from above is above all; the one who is of the earth belongs to the earth and speaks about earthly things. The one who comes from heaven is above all.
points.apply: Read one page of the Gospel slowly each day of the novena, and end with an act of faith in the Lord who speaks the words of God.

points.h: He gives the Spirit without measure
sub: The Ascension as the condition of the gift.
Nine days with Mary in the upper room.
From the pierced Heart, rivers of living water.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
points.apply: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each day until Pentecost, with Mary, and make the First Friday with confession and Holy Communion.

points.h: I press on toward the goal
sub: The upward call of God in Christ Jesus.
q: But those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.
I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Name one failure you keep carrying, give it to the Heart of Jesus, and do not take it with you into the novena.

concl: The Lord who has gone up is above all, and from his open Heart he gives the Spirit without measure.
With Mary in the upper room, let us pray, forget what lies behind and run toward the upward call.
2027-05-07.resolve: For these nine days, pray daily with Mary for the Holy Spirit, and let one old failure go into the Heart of Jesus.

intro: Theme: “He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.”
The second day of the novena: fruit worthy of repentance, the fire that winnows the heart, and the undivided devotion of which Mary is the model.

sub: A prophet speaking to his own people.
q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
points.apply: Choose one concrete fruit of conversion this week and do it before Pentecost.

q: But who can endure the day of his coming, and who can stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap.
He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
points.apply: In the novena each day, ask the Spirit to burn away one habit that is only chaff.

q: Teach me your way, O LORD, that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart to revere your name.
I say this for your own benefit, not to put any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
points.apply: Give the Lord one undivided hour this weekend, and pray with Mary for vocations and families.

concl: God looks for fruit, and the Spirit's fire makes the heart whole.
With Mary, let us pray for that fire in these days of waiting.
2027-05-08.resolve: This week, bear one fruit of conversion, give the Lord an undivided hour, and pray the novena daily with Mary.

intro: Theme: “The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
The fourth day of the novena: the Lord who asks for a drink, the living water of the Spirit, and the traditions through which that water has reached us.

q: O God, you are my God, I seek you, my soul thirsts for you; my flesh faints for you, as in a dry and weary land where there is no water.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water, and Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”
points.apply: Cross one wall this week by speaking kindly to someone your circle keeps at a distance.

sub: Every thirst is a thirst for God.
q: With joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.
The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.
points.apply: Each day of the novena, name your thirst before the Lord and ask him for the Spirit.

points.h: Stand firm and hold fast to the traditions
sub: By word of mouth and by letter.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
So then, brothers and sisters, stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught by us, either by word of mouth or by our letter.
points.apply: Teach a child one prayer of our Church this week, or explain one part of the Qurbana at home.

concl: The Lord who asked for water gives the Spirit, a spring that never runs dry.
Let us bring him our thirst and keep the faith handed down to us.
2027-05-10.resolve: This week, name your thirst before God, cross one wall, and hand on one prayer of our Church to a child.

intro: Theme: “So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.”
The fifth day of the novena: greed that poisons families, the fool who spoke only to himself, and the love that will not make a weaker brother stumble.

points.h: Life does not consist in possessions
sub: A family quarrel over an inheritance.
Greed that a fair division cannot cure.
q: The lover of money will not be satisfied with money; nor the lover of wealth, with gain. This also is vanity.
Take care! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; for one's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.
points.apply: Take one step toward peace in any family quarrel over land or money this week.

sub: The man who talked only to himself.
Goods that pass through our hands to God.
q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
So it is with those who store up treasures for themselves but are not rich toward God.
points.apply: Give away one thing you have stored and do not use, and set aside a share of your income for the poor.

points.h: Do not become a stumbling block
sub: The weak brother for whom Christ died.
q: You shall not revile the deaf or put a stumbling block before the blind; you shall fear your God: I am the LORD.
But take care that this liberty of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.
points.apply: Give up one habit or word that could make a younger or weaker person stumble.

concl: Our life is not in our barns, and our rights are given us for others.
In these days of waiting, let us empty our hands so that the Spirit may fill them.
2027-05-11.resolve: This week, make peace over property, give away what you hoard, and protect the faith of the weak.

intro: Theme: “And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.”
The sixth day of the novena: the prayer of the Hour that the Ascended Lord still prays, eternal life as knowing God, and the love poured out by the Spirit that casts out fear.

sub: The prayer answered at the Ascension.
The High Priest who still intercedes.
q: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you.
points.apply: Read John 17 a few verses each day this week, and join your prayer to the prayer of Jesus.

sub: To know, not only to know about.
Glorifying God by finishing our work.
q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes today speaking to Jesus as to a friend.

sub: The Spirit, the gift that makes love possible.
q: Do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
points.apply: Entrust one fear to God's love in the novena, and do one act of love for someone difficult.

concl: The Lord who prayed for us on the night before he died prays for us still, and gives us his Spirit of love.
To know him is eternal life; to love the brother is the proof that we know him.
2027-05-12.resolve: This week, pray John 17, speak to Jesus as a friend each day, and let love overcome one fear and one dislike.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
The seventh day of the novena: the word of life heard, seen and touched, the cost of following Christ to the end, and the salt that must not lose its taste.

sub: Fellowship with the Father and the Son.
q: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
We declare to you what was from the beginning, what we have heard, what we have seen with our eyes, what we have looked at and touched with our hands, concerning the word of life.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, simply, what Jesus has done in your life.

points.h: Carry the cross and follow me
sub: No love in the place of Christ.
q: Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from following you! Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
points.apply: Give God back his first place in one area where another love has pushed him aside.

points.h: Sit down and count the cost
q: You shall not omit from your grain offerings the salt of the covenant with your God; with all your offerings you shall offer salt.
Salt is good; but if salt has lost its taste, how can its saltiness be restored?
points.apply: Finish one Christian commitment you have left half done, and restore one family practice of prayer.

concl: The apostles touched the Word of life and handed him on to us; the Spirit gives us courage to follow him to the end.
With Mary, who paid the cost at the Cross, let us carry our cross and keep our salt.
2027-05-13.resolve: This week, bear witness once, put Christ first in one thing, finish one tower, and pray the rosary for peace.

intro: Theme: “And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias; and he was added to the eleven apostles.”
On the feast of St Matthias: the Twelve completed by a praying Church, the witness to the Resurrection, the God who looks on the heart, and the gentle yoke of Christ.

sub: A Church at prayer with Mary.
Not whom we prefer, but whom you have chosen.
The quiet peace of Joseph Justus.
q: for the LORD does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
points.apply: Pray before every important decision this week, asking the Lord to show you what he has chosen.

sub: The Twelve for the new Israel.
The lot that falls on Matthias.
q: The lot is cast into the lap, but the decision is the LORD’s alone.
And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell on Matthias; and he was added to the eleven apostles.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, simply, why you believe that Jesus is risen.

sub: The youngest son, keeping the sheep.
Not many wise, not many powerful.
q: There remains yet the youngest, but he is keeping the sheep.
But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;
points.apply: Give your attention and respect to someone usually overlooked in your family, parish or workplace.

points.h: Come to me, and learn from me
q: but those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength,
Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Spend some minutes before the tabernacle this week, waiting for the Holy Spirit with Mary.

concl: The Lord who completed the Twelve by choosing Matthias still chooses, not by appearance, but by the heart.
Let us pray like the first Church, accept God's choices with peace, and witness to the Risen Lord as we wait for the Spirit.
2027-05-14.resolve: This week, pray before deciding, honour someone overlooked, and tell one person of your faith in the Risen Lord.

intro: Theme: “The threshing floors shall be full of grain, the vats shall overflow with wine and oil.”
On the feast of Mary, Protectress of Harvest, the eve of Pentecost: the festival of harvest, the promised Spirit, God's faithful gifts, and the Mother who watches over the little ones.

sub: Fifty days and the first fruits.
The first harvest of the Church.
q: You shall count until the day after the seventh sabbath, fifty days; then you shall present an offering of new grain to the LORD.
So those who welcomed his message were baptized, and that day about three thousand persons were added.
points.apply: Offer God the first fruits of your week: your first hour of each day, given to prayer.

points.h: I will pour out my spirit on all flesh
sub: Sons and daughters, old and young.
Mary, first to receive the Spirit's fullness.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, as well as his brothers.
points.apply: Pray tonight with your family for the coming of the Holy Spirit, asking Mary to pray with you.

points.h: The gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable
sub: Israel, beloved for the sake of the ancestors.
q: The LORD will give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
points.apply: Thank God for one gift he has never taken back from you, even when you were unfaithful.

points.h: Not one of these little ones lost
sub: Their angels see the Father's face.
The Mother who prays by name.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
So it is not the will of your Father in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
points.apply: Pray the rosary this week for one person who has drifted away, and reach out to them.

concl: The Protectress of Harvest leads us from the fields to the upper room, from the harvest of grain to the harvest of the Spirit.
With her let us bring our first fruits, wait for the rain of the Spirit, and search for every little one.
2027-05-15.resolve: This week, give God the first hour of each day, forgive from the heart, and pray by name for one who has gone astray.

intro: Theme: “for God is a God not of disorder but of peace.”
On the day of Mary, Mother of the Church: the Mother given from the Cross, an assembly built up in peace, and the gentle and humble heart of Christ.

sub: The beloved disciple and all disciples.
Mother of the whole people of God.
q: The man named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of all living.
Then he said to the disciple, “Here is your mother.”
points.apply: Entrust your family to the Mother of the Church with a decade of the rosary each day this week.

points.h: Let all things be done for building up
sub: Each in turn, listening to one another.
Mary's silence and her few words.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Let all things be done for building up.
points.apply: In every meeting and discussion this week, speak only what builds up.

points.h: Learn from me, gentle and humble in heart
sub: The humble servant of the Lord.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you;
Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me; for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
points.apply: Visit or call one person who is carrying a heavy burden, and bring them the comfort of Christ.

concl: The Church born at Pentecost begins her journey with her Mother, who teaches her to listen, to build up and to be humble.
With Mary, let us bring every burden to the gentle heart of her Son.
2027-05-17.resolve: This week, pray a daily decade with your family, speak only words that build up, and comfort one who is weary.

intro: Theme: “Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes. Immediately they regained their sight and followed him.”
The stubborn prayer of the blind, the compassion that touches and opens the eyes, and a Church made worthy of its call.

points.h: Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David
sub: Blind, but not deaf to his passing.
The crowd that says, Be quiet.
q: the LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer every day this week, morning and evening.

points.h: What do you want me to do for you?
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped;
Jesus stood still and called them, saying, “What do you want me to do for you?”
points.apply: Tell Jesus honestly, in a quiet moment, the one thing you most need from him.

q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end;
To this end we always pray for you, asking that our God will make you worthy of his call and will fulfill by his power every good resolve and work of faith,
points.apply: Pray by name this week for three people in your parish, that God may make them worthy of his call.

concl: The Lord who stood still for the blind of Jericho stands still for us, opens our eyes and calls us to follow.
Let us follow him with faith that grows and love that increases, steadfast in every trial.
2027-05-18.resolve: This week, pray the Jesus Prayer daily, name your need to the Lord, and pray for the persecuted and for your parish.

intro: Theme: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that someone took and sowed in his field;”
The Church growing from small beginnings, the hidden yeast that changes the world, and a Eucharistic community that waits for one another.

points.h: The smallest of all the seeds
sub: One hundred and twenty in an upper room.
The tree where the birds nest.
q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live;
it is the smallest of all the seeds, but when it has grown it is the greatest of shrubs and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and make nests in its branches.
points.apply: Begin one small, faithful practice this week and keep it every day.

q: For whoever has despised the day of small things shall rejoice,
The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and mixed in with three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of goodness each day this week at your work or school, without telling anyone.

q: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts.
So then, my brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience before your next Holy Communion, and go to confession if you need to.

concl: The Church of the apostles grows like a seed and works like yeast, and her heart is a table where all wait for one another.
Let us be faithful in small things, hidden and active in the world, and prepared at the altar.
2027-05-19.resolve: This week, keep one small daily practice, do one hidden good deed each day, and prepare well for Holy Communion.

intro: Theme: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
The new covenant written by the Spirit on our hearts, the zeal of Jesus for his Father's house, and the Risen Body of Christ, the true Temple in which we are living stones.

points.h: I will write it on their hearts
sub: The Spirit poured out at Pentecost.
A covenant that begins with forgiveness.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit each morning this week to write one commandment on your heart as a law of love.

sub: The market in the Temple courts.
The whip of cords and the overturned tables.
Love that cleanses what it loves.
q: It is zeal for your house that has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
He told those who were selling the doves, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father’s house a marketplace!”
points.apply: Overturn one table this week: a habit of greed, bargaining with God or noise that keeps you from prayer.

sub: Destroyed on the Cross, raised on the third day.
We are God's temple, and the Spirit dwells in us.
q: Then he brought me back to the entrance of the temple; there, water was flowing from below the threshold of the temple toward the east (for the temple faced east); and the water was flowing down from below the south end of the threshold of the temple, south of the altar.
Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that God’s Spirit dwells in you?
points.apply: Come early to the Sunday Qurbana and spend five minutes in silence, offering yourself as his temple.

concl: The Spirit writes on our hearts the law that Christ fulfilled, and makes us living stones of the Temple that rose on the third day.
Let us keep the house of God, and our own hearts, as houses of prayer.
2027-05-20.resolve: This week, ask the Spirit to write one commandment on your heart, overturn one table of greed, and pray daily for our Synod of Bishops.

intro: Theme: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.”
The Friday of Gold: Isaiah's Holy Way, the lame man raised at the Beautiful Gate, the more excellent way of love, and the compassion of Jesus at the gate of Nain.

sub: A desert in bloom and the Holy Way.
The lame who leap like a deer.
q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
Therefore lift your drooping hands and strengthen your weak knees,
points.apply: Visit or call one person who is weak, sick or discouraged, and strengthen them with your presence.

points.h: What I have I give you
sub: The hour of prayer and the Beautiful Gate.
Look at us: a gaze that lifts up.
The Name of Jesus, richer than gold.
q: He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap,
But Peter said, “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.”
points.apply: Give one gift this week that costs no money: time, attention or prayer in Jesus' Name.

q: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can floods drown it. If one offered for love all the wealth of one’s house, it would be utterly scorned.
And now faith, hope, and love abide, these three; and the greatest of these is love.
points.apply: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4–7 each evening this week and examine your day by it.

points.h: Young man, I say to you, rise
sub: A widow at the gate of Nain.
The signs of the One who is to come.
q: then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy. For waters shall break forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert;

And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.”
points.apply: Help your parish make one concrete step for the disabled or the grieving: a ramp, a visit, a meal.

concl: The Church has no gold of her own; she has the Name of Jesus and the love of the Spirit, and these are enough to raise the lame.
Let us look at those at the gate, take their hand and give them what we have.
2027-05-21.resolve: This week, strengthen one weak person, give one gift that costs no money, and pray 1 Corinthians 13 each evening.

intro: Theme: “This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent.”
The Church, the one Body of Christ with many members, each placed by God, and faith as the first work, learnt with the Blessed Virgin Mary.

sub: Baptized into one Body, made to drink of one Spirit.
The Church, the Body of the Risen Lord.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so it is with Christ.
points.apply: Pray this week for someone in your parish with whom you find unity difficult.

points.h: As God arranged, as he chose
sub: The foot that envies the hand.
The eye that despises the ear.
No one in the Body by accident.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But as it is, God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.
points.apply: Offer one hour of service to your parish this month, in the place where help is needed.

sub: Working for the food of eternal life.
Faith, the work of God, with Mary.
q: Why do you spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and delight yourselves in rich food.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For it is on him that God the Father has set his seal.
points.apply: Before each meal this week, ask for the bread that endures for eternal life, and receive the Qurbana with renewed faith.

concl: We are one Body in Christ, each member placed by God and needed by all.
Let us seek Jesus for himself, and believe in the One whom the Father has sent.
2027-05-22.resolve: This week, find your place of service in the parish, thank one hidden member, and pray a decade of the rosary for the unity of the Church.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,”
Faith handed on by imitation, our citizenship in heaven and the body of glory, and Martha's confession at the graveside of Lazarus.

sub: Faith passed on from life to life.
q: Now if you are unwilling to serve the LORD, choose this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your ancestors served in the region beyond the River or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living; but as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD.
Brothers and sisters, join in imitating me, and observe those who live according to the example you have in us.
points.apply: Let a younger person see you pray this week, and speak to them of what faith means to you.

sub: Enemies of the Cross, wept over.
The colony and the greater city.
The body of our humiliation and the body of glory.
