q: How lovely is your dwelling place, O LORD of hosts! My soul longs, indeed it faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
But our citizenship is in heaven, and it is from there that we are expecting a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Before one purchase or decision this week, ask whether it suits a citizen of heaven.

points.h: I am the resurrection and the life
sub: The last day brought into the present.
q: Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord GOD: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people; and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,
points.apply: Visit or call one grieving person, and pray with them for their beloved dead.

concl: We are citizens of heaven, waiting for the Saviour who will transform our lowly bodies; the Resurrection already stands before us in the Person of Jesus.
Let us live lives worth imitating, and answer him with Martha: Yes, Lord, I believe.
2027-05-24.resolve: This week, let your faith be seen by a younger person, pray for one who has drifted from the Church, and bring comfort to a grieving family.

intro: Theme: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
Paul's apostleship sealed by a living Church, his rights laid aside so that nothing may block the Gospel, and Peter's loyal faith when many walk away from the Bread of Life.

sub: An encounter with the Risen Lord.
Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel.
q: If I say, “I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,” then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot.
If I proclaim the gospel, this gives me no ground for boasting, for an obligation is laid on me, and woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
points.apply: Speak of your faith this week to one person who does not know Christ well.

sub: The ox that treads the grain.
q: You shall not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.

If others share this rightful claim on you, do not we still more? Nevertheless, we have not made use of this right, but we endure anything rather than put an obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.
points.apply: Give generously to the missions of our Church, and give up one right this week for the sake of peace.

points.h: Lord, to whom can we go?
sub: The hard saying about his Body and Blood.
q: Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth that I desire other than you.
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
points.apply: Visit the Blessed Sacrament before Thursday's feast, and pray for one person who has left the Church.

concl: The apostles were sent by the Risen Lord and gave up their rights so that the Gospel might run unhindered; Peter stayed when many left, because only Jesus has the words of eternal life.
Let us stay with him, support his mission and prepare our hearts for the feast of his Body and Blood.
2027-05-25.resolve: This week, speak of Christ to one person, give generously to the missions, and make a visit to the Blessed Sacrament before Thursday.

intro: Theme: “Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away.”
The open door of Jesus, the Father who draws us, and the body as a temple of the Holy Spirit destined to rise.

points.h: Anyone who comes to me I will never drive away
sub: The Father's will to lose no one.
The door that is never shut.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you.
Everything that the Father gives me will come to me, and anyone who comes to me I will never drive away;
points.apply: Go to confession this week if you have stayed away, trusting the open door.

points.h: Drawn by the Father, raised on the last day
sub: The Father draws those we pray for.
The bread of life, pledge of the resurrection.
q: Therefore prophesy, and say to them, Thus says the Lord God: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people; and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
This is indeed the will of my Father, that all who see the Son and believe in him may have eternal life; and I will raise them up on the last day.
points.apply: Name one person each day this week and ask the Father to draw them to his Son.

points.h: A temple of the Holy Spirit
sub: The body is for the Lord.
q: then the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and the man became a living being.
Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, which you have from God, and that you are not your own?
points.apply: Choose one discipline this week that honours your body as the Spirit's temple.

concl: Jesus never drives away anyone who comes; the Father is drawing us and those we love.
The Spirit of Pentecost lives in our bodies: let us keep the temple holy until the Lord raises it on the last day.
2027-05-26.resolve: This week, come back to the Lord in confession if needed, pray daily for one person by name, and keep one discipline for the sake of the temple.

intro: Theme: “I am the living bread that came down from heaven. Whoever eats of this bread will live forever; and the bread that I will give for the life of the world is my flesh.”
On the Feast of the Body and Blood of Christ: the bread and wine of Melchizedek, the pure offering foretold by Malachi, the tradition handed on by Paul, and the true food and drink of the Gospel.

sub: A priest-king who comes from nowhere.
Blessing in the name of God Most High.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
points.apply: Pray this week for your parish priest and for vocations to the priesthood.

points.h: A pure offering in every place
sub: Better to shut the doors than to worship carelessly.
From the rising of the sun to its setting.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering; for my name is great among the nations, says the Lord of hosts.
And it is by God’s will that we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
points.apply: Come early to the Sunday Qurbana, and stay to the end with a moment of thanksgiving.

sub: Do this in remembrance of me.
Examine yourselves and discern the Body.
q: This day shall be a day of remembrance for you. You shall celebrate it as a festival to the Lord; throughout your generations you shall observe it as a perpetual ordinance.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
points.apply: Before your next Communion, examine your conscience and, if needed, go to confession.

sub: How can this man give us his flesh?
Unless you eat, you have no life.
Abiding in him, carrying him out.
q: When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, “It is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
Those who eat my flesh and drink my blood abide in me, and I in them.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes in adoration this week, or join the Eucharistic procession of your parish.

concl: The priest of Melchizedek's order offers himself in every place: the Holy Qurbana is the pure offering and the true food of the Church.
Let us discern his Body, come to him with clean hearts, and carry him into our homes and streets.
2027-05-27.resolve: This week, prepare for Communion with an examination of conscience, spend fifteen minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, and pray for priests.

intro: Theme: “Very truly, I tell you, whoever believes has eternal life. I am the bread of life.”
Taught by God at the table of the Word, fed with the bread of life, and belonging wholly to Christ.

points.h: They shall all be taught by God
sub: Only the Son has seen the Father.
q: All your children shall be taught by the Lord, and great shall be the prosperity of your children.
It is written in the prophets, ‘And they shall all be taught by God.’ Everyone who has heard and learned from the Father comes to me.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel at home before the Qurbana this week.

points.h: I am the bread of life
q: Mortals ate of the bread of angels; he sent them food in abundance.
This is the bread that comes down from heaven, so that one may eat of it and not die.
points.apply: Make a spiritual communion each day this week when you cannot go to the Qurbana.

sub: All is yours, and you are Christ's.
q: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not rely on your own insight.
If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord; so then, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord’s.
points.apply: Make peace with someone with whom you have quarrelled over a preacher, a priest or a parish matter.

concl: God teaches us at the table of the Word and feeds us at the table of the Body and Blood.
We belong to no party but to Christ, the bread of life, who belongs to the Father.
2027-05-28.resolve: This week, prepare for Sunday by reading the Gospel, make a daily spiritual communion, and make peace where you have taken sides.

intro: Theme: “Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.”
Five barley loaves in the Lord's hands, the fragments gathered so that nothing is lost, and the one bread that makes us one body.

points.h: Five barley loaves and two fish
sub: What are they among so many?
He took, gave thanks and distributed.
Our small offering at every Qurbana.
q: He set it before them, they ate, and had some left, according to the word of the Lord.
There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish. But what are they among so many people?
points.apply: Give one small, concrete gift to the Lord this week, without waiting until it is enough.

points.h: So that nothing may be lost
sub: The king who will not be made by bread.
q: You shall eat your fill and bless the Lord your God for the good land that he has given you.
When they were satisfied, he told his disciples, “Gather up the fragments left over, so that nothing may be lost.”
points.apply: Waste no food this week, and share what is left over.

sub: The cup of blessing and the bread we break.
Communion sends us to the poor.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
points.apply: Name one idol that competes for your heart, and put it down before the Lord in confession or prayer.

concl: The Lord takes our little and feeds many; he gathers the fragments so that nothing and no one is lost.
The one bread makes us one body: no divided heart, and no one forgotten.
2027-05-29.resolve: This week, give one small gift, waste no food, and turn away from one idol that competes with God.

intro: Theme: “And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.”
On the feast of the Visitation, at the close of the month of Mary: the haste of love, the joy of the unborn Baptist, the Mother of my Lord, and faith that becomes genuine love.

sub: The road to the hill country.
Not anxiety, but the haste of love.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
In those days Mary set out and went with haste to a Judean town in the hill country,
points.apply: Visit someone who needs you this week, without postponing it.

sub: Elizabeth's words in our Hail Mary.
q: David danced before the Lord with all his might; David was girded with a linen ephod.
For as soon as I heard the sound of your greeting, the child in my womb leaped for joy.
points.apply: Pray one decade of the Rosary slowly each day this week.

sub: The new ark of the covenant.
q: David was afraid of the Lord that day; he said, “How can the ark of the Lord come into my care?”
And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
points.apply: After Communion this week, pray Elizabeth's words as your thanksgiving.

q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
love one another with mutual affection; outdo one another in showing honor.
points.apply: Choose one phrase of Romans 12:9–16 and live it concretely this week.

concl: Mary believed the word of the Lord and set out in haste to serve, carrying Christ to Elizabeth's house.
At the close of her month, the best homage we can give her is to believe as she did and to go as she went.
2027-05-31.resolve: This week, make one visit you have postponed, pray the Rosary slowly, and live one phrase of Romans 12 for someone in need.
